title: The Seventh Bell · revision 6
summary:
Revision 6 of The Seventh Bell, for Waypoint 1.34.

- **Corvane is part of the Forgotten Realms.** It lies far out in the Trackless Sea behind the Stormwall. The Wrongweather opened the Seam thirty years ago (382 SS, 1462 DR), and Sword Coast ships have been arriving ever since.
- **Pellmoor Landing.** Pellmoor is now Corvane's only lawful port: the Quays, the Tally, Strangers' Row, and the old ferry village on the Old Shore. Five new NPCs and a new faction, the Landing.
- **Memory as money.** Motes, keeps, heartkeeps and knowings circulate alongside gold, with table rules and a memory ledger.
- **Foresight playbook.** 209 prepared plays across 32 chapters and 38 anytime plays, each with what to say, what to do, the 2024 rules involved, and what it changes now and later; 54 tracked world-state facts; 32 session prep briefs; 32 encounters; 22 Corvane stat blocks built on the 2024 Monster Manual; and an ending forecast.
- **D&D 2024 throughout,** with the updated wiki pages marked v6.

Your notes, IsoForge map kits, chronicle and any world state you have recorded are kept. Replaced wiki text moves to each page's revision history.

edits.replace:
They trade memories as money, and lately for gold. They have forgotten what the bells sounded like.

For four centuries a wall of storm at sea hid Corvane from the rest of the world. Thirty years ago a passage opened, and ships from Faerûn's Sword Coast began to arrive. They anchor at Pellmoor, on the still waters of the Mute Mere, now the busiest port in Corvane.

edits.find: > "The fog lifts off the Mute Mere in long grey ribbons, and the village of Pellmoor comes into sight: reed roofs, leaning docks, nets like the sails of drowned ships. The chapel bell is silent. A girl stands on the ferry-dock, staring at the water with her hands folded tight. She does not look up when you arrive. She says, without turning: *'Are you here for the tongue, or for the bell?'*"
edits.replace: > "The fog lifts off the Mute Mere in long gray ribbons, and Pellmoor Landing comes into sight: forty masts standing over water so still the ships look painted on it, and beneath them, just under the surface, the rooftops of a drowned town. On the Quays, a dozen languages argue over the price of a memory. Past the last warehouse, the old reed-roofed ferry village still leans toward the water as if none of this were happening. A girl stands on the oldest dock, staring at the water with her hands folded tight. She does not look up when you arrive. She says, without turning: *'Are you here for the tongue, or for the bell?'*"

plays.title: They speak gently to Ila
plays.why: Ila is fourteen, alone on the old dock, and asks the first question; most tables answer kindly.
plays.readAloud: "It's warm. Not like a hot pan. Like something alive that's been asleep. When it hums, the water on the far shore ripples in the shape of a bell. I've seen it. Nobody believes me except Mother Sallow, and she only believes me because she's scared."
plays.response: Ila unwraps the oilskin for whoever asked respectfully. The Tongue hums while she holds it and fades when she sets it down. She answers one plain question per kindness, then asks: "Did you hear it too?" Mother Sallow is watching from the net-racks and walks over once Ila smiles.
plays.consequence: Ila trusts this person. She will show them the Tongue again and tell them when the Hushmen come.
plays.fallback: If the table freezes, Ila counts the masts on the Quays out loud and asks which ship they came on.
plays.tells: A player crouches to her level, offers food or a coat, or answers her question honestly.
plays.rules: No check: Ila is willing (2024 Influence). A Bell-Touched character recognises the hum at once.
plays.later: S3: Ila insists on a say in what happens to the Tongue. S28: she remembers who was kind first.
plays.keywords: ila, girl, dock, kind, gentle, talk, tongue, hum, show, child

plays.title: They brush Ila off or demand the Tongue
plays.why: Some characters arrive on business and treat the strange child as a nuisance.
plays.readAloud: Mother Sallow's voice cuts across the dock like a dropped oar. "She's a child. You can be a child too, or you can be useful."
plays.response: Ila turns away and pockets the bundle. Mother Sallow plants herself between them and gives the party one chance: find the eastern-marsh ferry that has been missing a week, and she'll believe they mean well. She never raises her voice twice.
plays.consequence: Ila will not show the Tongue today. The missing ferry (H-02) becomes the party's way back in.
plays.fallback: If nobody takes the ferry job, a ferry-folk widow begs them at the Shuttered Bell instead.
plays.tells: Players talk over her, laugh at the question, or ask what she's hiding.
plays.rules: Mother Sallow starts Indifferent (2024 Influence). Charm moves her nowhere; blunt honesty makes her Friendly.
plays.later: S2: Sallow's help costs more; she asks them to speak a dead person's name on the Memory Shore first. S3: Ila argues against handing them the Tongue.
plays.keywords: rude, ignore, demand, push, threaten, mother sallow, sallow, ferry job

plays.title: They try to take or steal the Tongue from Ila
plays.why: A rogue sees a humming relic and a child holding it.
plays.readAloud: Ila's hand closes on empty oilskin. She doesn't scream at first. She just looks at you, and then the whole Old Shore goes quiet, the way water goes quiet before something surfaces.
plays.response: Use your session-zero boundaries; no harm to Ila is enacted if that is a Line. A lifted bundle is noticed: ferry-folk step out of every doorway, Brannagh Wick sends a runner to the Pilots' Hall, and Mother Sallow demands it back. If they keep it, the Old Shore closes to them: no ferries, no pilots, no hymn.
plays.consequence: The party holds the Tongue and has lost the ferry-folk. Quill hears of it by evening.
plays.fallback: If they return it within the day with an honest apology, Mother Sallow lets it be known they did.
plays.tells: A player asks where Ila sleeps, how she carries it, or rolls Sleight of Hand.
plays.rules: Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Ila's Passive Perception 15 (she has Advantage near water, +5 passive).
plays.later: S2: without the response hymn the Night Song is dangerous and the Cantor treats them as the forgetful. S3: Mother Sallow will not open her ledger to them. S4: Quill's report names them as thieves.
plays.keywords: steal, take, grab, snatch, pickpocket, sleight of hand, rob, ila

plays.title: They accept Mother Sallow's three-day bargain
plays.why: Sallow offers what the party wants (answers) for something easy to promise (keep the Tongue safe).
plays.readAloud: "Keep it safe for three days. Not from thieves. From the Court. Do that, and I'll tell you what the water knows. And learn this, before the dark comes: when they sing, you sing back."
plays.response: Over bitter reed tea she explains that the Mere holds the dead and the Tongue belongs to Ossa, the Bone Bell. She cannot say why she has no memory of her husband's face. She teaches the response to the Night Song: a two-line call and answer. Ask each player, "What do you want from Mother Sallow?" She answers honestly but not fully; she knows the Drowned are her ancestors.
plays.consequence: The party has a promise to keep and the response hymn. Record the bargain.
plays.fallback: If they dither, she hands Ila the tea and says, "Then I'll keep it, and you can watch me fail."
plays.tells: Players ask what she knows about the Drowned, the bell, or Ila's father.
plays.rules: Learning the hymn takes a few minutes and no check. Singing it later quiets the Drowned for one hour (v5 2.11).
plays.later: S2: the hymn calms the Night Song for an hour. S3: if they kept the Tongue from the Court for three days, she opens the ledger to them without being asked.
plays.keywords: mother sallow, bargain, deal, three days, tea, hymn, response, night song, keep it safe

plays.title: They hand the Tongue to Quill
plays.why: Quill is polite, official, and offers an easy way out of trouble.
plays.readAloud: Quill takes the bundle in both gloved hands, and the hum stops dead, as if someone had put a palm on a bell. "Thank you. The Court remembers its friends." He writes in his ledger without looking down.
plays.response: Quill gives a grey-wax receipt and a Tithe-exemption chit for one mote, records every face, and leaves for the Landing House that night. Ila does not cry. She walks to the end of the old dock and sits there until dark.
plays.consequence: The Court holds Ossa's Tongue and knows the party's faces.
plays.fallback: If a player regrets it at once, Quill is still on the Quays for an hour, haggling with a Coster clerk.
plays.tells: Players ask whether giving it up would protect Ila, or what the Court pays.
plays.later: S3: returning it to the Mere now means recovering it first. S4: Maudrin already holds it and offers Ila's Tithe-exemption instead; she mentions the party by name. Concord: Ossa needs the Tongue back (the Tidewarden ferries the Ringer once the party holds it again).
plays.keywords: quill, give, hand over, surrender, court, tongue, receipt, comply

plays.title: They lie to Quill
plays.why: Most parties protect the child and bluff the official.
plays.readAloud: Quill nods along, then asks one quiet question and waits. "Where did the child's coat go?"
plays.response: Quill is not a fool. He asks exactly one specific question and lets the silence work. If the party can't answer, he says, "Then I'll look myself," and searches the Old Shore that night with his guard. He finds the Tongue unless it has been moved; a hiding place on the Quays or aboard a foreign ship is outside his warrant.
plays.consequence: Quill is suspicious. A search happens tonight unless the lie holds.
plays.fallback: If the scene stalls, Quill's guard spots Ila's oversized ferry coat on a peg.
plays.tells: A player says they know nothing about any humming, or offers a cover story.
plays.rules: Charisma (Deception) against Quill's Passive Insight 13. On a success he leaves suspicious but without cause to search.
plays.later: If he finds it: as handing it over, and S4's Gate Clerk raises Persuasion DCs by 2. If the lie holds: Quill returns in S3 with a second Hushman.
plays.keywords: lie, bluff, deceive, cover story, deny, quill, hide, coat

plays.title: They attack Quill
plays.why: A Hushman threatening a child is an easy villain for a level-1 party.
plays.readAloud: Quill steps back so neatly it looks rehearsed. His gloves come up grey and silent. "You've made yourselves a Tithe-case. I do hope you understand what that means."
plays.response: Run Quill's patrol. Quill wants an arrest, not a killing; his guard fights while Quill retreats toward the Landing House shouting for witnesses. Foreign captains on the Quays will not interfere with the Court. Ila's house becomes the first place the Hushmen search.
plays.consequence: The party is a Tithe-case. The Landing House's six Hushmen now watch the Old Shore.
plays.fallback: If a PC drops, Quill has them bound, not killed, and offers them back for the Tongue.
plays.tells: Hands on weapons; a player asks how many Hushmen are in Pellmoor.
plays.rules: Encounter: Quill's patrol. Silence-glove strikes make no sound and can't be sensed by Tonework.
plays.later: Tonight: the Hushmen raid Ila's house (run it). S3: Quill's report reaches Hallowmere, but the Chancellor's invitation still comes; the Court prefers to buy before it threatens. S4: the Gate Clerk already has their names.
plays.keywords: attack, fight, kill, hit, quill, hushman, guard, violence, combat

plays.title: They bribe Quill
plays.why: Quill is short on quota and visibly open to an arrangement.
plays.readAloud: Quill looks at the gold the way a man looks at a fine meal he isn't allowed to eat. "Gold I can't put on a shelf, friend. But I'll take it. And one more thing. A name."
plays.response: Quill pockets gold for himself, but his quota needs memories. He asks for one favor: a name of someone 'not keeping the Court's quiet.' If they give Mother Sallow's, he writes it down. If they refuse, he keeps the coin and says, "Then I'll remember you were generous."
plays.consequence: Quill is bribed. He leaves the Tongue alone for now.
plays.fallback: If they won't name anyone, Quill suggests the quota itself: 'Three memories, freely given. I'm not particular whose.'
plays.tells: A player jingles coin, asks what his quota is, or offers a 'gift'.
plays.rules: No check for the bribe. A Charisma (Persuasion) Influence check, DC 15, talks him out of the name if they offer something else useful.
plays.later: If they named Mother Sallow: Hushmen question her in S2 and her ledger is at risk in S3. If they refused: in S4 Quill's letter to the gate vouches for them (Gate Clerk DCs drop by 2).
plays.keywords: bribe, pay, gold, coin, buy off, deal, quill, money

plays.title: They fill the village's memory quota themselves
plays.why: H-03 makes the quota a problem; v6 makes gold useless for it, so the only gift that works is a memory.
plays.readAloud: "Three memories," Quill says, already uncapping a keep-glass. "The Court is not particular whose. That's rather the point of the Court."
plays.response: Gold cannot pay a Corvanese subject's Tithe (that's gilding, and illegal), but nothing stops the party giving memories of their own on the villagers' behalf. Quill draws each one with a tuning fork in about a minute. The three villagers he was hounding are Bellwright sympathisers, and they will not forget this.
plays.consequence: Pellmoor's quota is met. Quill leaves satisfied. Three households owe the party.
plays.fallback: If the party offers gold instead, Reckoner Sela Maunt quietly explains why that won't work, and what will.
plays.tells: Players ask why villagers won't pay, or offer to cover the shortfall.
plays.rules: Each giver names the memory and its weight (mote, keep or heartkeep) in the Memory Ledger. The DM may award Heroic Inspiration for a memory given freely to someone who needs it.
plays.later: S3: those households warn the party when Hushmen move and can hide Ila. S4 (siege): they shelter villagers. S10: a Bellwright contact knows the party's names kindly.
plays.keywords: quota, tithe, pay the quota, give memories, gilding, villagers, h-03, sacrifice, keep, mote

plays.title: They take the Tongue to the Quays to learn what it's worth
plays.why: A port full of Reckoners and foreign buyers invites appraisal.
plays.readAloud: Sela Maunt doesn't touch it. She taps one tuning fork on the counter and the fork goes silent mid-note. "That's not a memory, love. That's a bell. Put it away before someone who isn't me sees it."
plays.response: Sela refuses to appraise it and warns them to hide it. Too late: Master Orsolo Venn, two stalls over, heard the fork die. He introduces himself warmly, offers 600 gp and a berth home on the Coster ship Gilded Heron, and gives them three days to think.
plays.consequence: Venn knows the Tongue exists and wants it. He pays Quill, so Quill will hear by evening.
plays.fallback: If they avoid Venn, he sends a polite note to the Shuttered Bell with his offer in writing.
plays.tells: Players ask who in Pellmoor would know about relics, or head for the Reckoning House.
plays.later: S1: Quill arrives on the first evening instead of the second. S3: Venn's offer becomes a real option (sell it abroad). If they refuse him twice, he tries to buy it from Ila directly.
plays.keywords: appraise, sell, worth, value, reckoner, reckoning house, sela, venn, merchant, quays, buyer

plays.title: A Stormborn character asks to travel inland
plays.why: Faerûnian characters arrive under the Landing Charter and will soon want to leave Pellmoor.
plays.readAloud: The Landing House clerk stamps your papers without reading them. "Landing due, five gold. Pellmoor and the Mere road only. Anywhere else needs a writ from Hallowmere. They take about a season. Next."
plays.response: Explain the Landing Charter plainly: foreigners trade freely here but need a Court writ of passage to go inland. Quill can 'expedite' one for a heartkeep, and means it. Brannagh Wick knows ferry routes that skirt the Mere road checkpoints. Don't block the plot: the Chancellor's letter at the end of Session 3 counts as a writ.
plays.consequence: The party understands the Court controls movement, and that a writ is worth something.
plays.fallback: If a player feels trapped, Dorra Pell mentions that 'writs have a way of arriving for interesting people.'
plays.tells: A player from the Sword Coast asks about Hallowmere, roads, or the rest of Corvane.
plays.later: S3: the Chancellor's invitation sets the writ to 'invited'. S4: the Hallowmere gate checks it. A forged writ works until someone checks the grey wax (DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) for a Hushman).
plays.keywords: writ, passage, papers, landing house, travel, inland, hallowmere, faerunian, stormborn, charter, customs

plays.title: They cast Detect Magic or Identify on the Tongue
plays.why: Level-1 casters reach for Detect Magic the moment something hums.
plays.readAloud: The spell doesn't find an aura so much as an answer. The Tongue hums back at you, one clean note, the way a glass rings when you speak near it.
plays.response: Detect Magic shows a faint aura that belongs to no school. Identify (or a minute's Study) reveals: 'Ossa's Tongue. It belongs to a bell under water.' Nothing about Tolls, and nothing about the Key. A Bell-Touched character recognises it without magic.
plays.consequence: The party knows what it is and where it belongs.
plays.fallback: If no one has the spell, Mother Sallow simply tells them.
plays.tells: A wizard, cleric or bard asks to cast a ritual on it.
plays.rules: Detect Magic (ritual) or Identify. Study action, Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) DC 12, for the same answer without a spell.
plays.later: S2: they may think to bring it on the dive. S3: returning it to the Mere becomes an informed choice.
plays.keywords: detect magic, identify, arcana, study, what is it, magic, aura, spell, ritual

plays.title: They defend Ila's house during the night raid
plays.why: v5 ends Session 1 with a Hushmen raid on the Harrow house if Quill suspects anything.
plays.readAloud: No knock. Just the door, opening very quietly, and two grey gloves catching the lamplight.
plays.response: Two Hushmen (Quill stays outside if he has already fought). They want the Tongue and the child's father's papers, and they withdraw when one drops or the alarm rouses the Old Shore. Ila can be hidden: under the net-racks, or with Brannagh at the Pilots' Hall.
plays.consequence: The Court's first move has failed or succeeded in front of the whole Old Shore.
plays.fallback: If the party is elsewhere, Ila hides on her own and finds them before dawn, shaking and furious.
plays.tells: The party keeps watch at the Harrow house, or asks where Ila sleeps tonight.
plays.rules: Encounter: the night raid. Hiding Ila: Dexterity (Stealth) DC 12 with the Hide action's rules; the ferry-folk help (Help action) without being asked.
plays.later: If the raid fails: S3 Quill brings reinforcements and the ferry-folk start to trust the party. If Ila is taken: she is held at the Landing House overnight and sent to Hallowmere at dawn (S3: a rescue on the Mere road).
plays.keywords: raid, night, defend, protect, hushmen, harrow house, ila, guard, ambush

sessions.summary: A port of forty masts on a drowned town, a girl on the oldest dock, and a bronze tongue that hums.

plays.title: They sing the response to the Night Song
plays.why: Mother Sallow taught it for exactly this, and the whole village does it.
plays.readAloud: Up and down the shore, people hum back at the water, the way you'd hum to a child who won't sleep. When you join them, the voice under the Mere hesitates, and for a while the names stop.
plays.response: The Night Song quiets for one hour. The Drowned do not attack the grieving or the singing. A character who sings with a dead person in mind feels the water listen; mark them, because the Cantor will ask about it.
plays.consequence: One safe hour on or near the water.
plays.fallback: If nobody learned it, Ila sings it, badly, and the Mere listens anyway.
plays.tells: Players ask what the villagers are humming, or if anyone remembers Sallow's hymn.
plays.rules: No check. A sincere attempt works; a Charisma (Performance) roll is flavour only and cannot fail.
plays.later: S2: the Cantor greets a singer more gently. S3: safe passage to the belfry is easier for anyone who has sung the response.
plays.keywords: sing, hymn, response, night song, hum, choir, drowned, calm, quiet

plays.title: They stay on the Memory Shore all night
plays.why: Curious characters want to hear the whole song.
plays.readAloud: Somewhere before dawn the cold stops mattering. You are standing on a ferry in fog, and your hands are someone else's hands.
plays.response: Each character who stays the full night makes the save. On a failure, roll on the Mere Memory table (v5 Part 11.4). If the party is investigating Tam, replace the roll for one character with Tam's last night: grey gloves, an emptied gaze, a boat drifting with no cargo.
plays.consequence: Someone carries a stranger's memory, possibly Tam's.
plays.fallback: If nobody fails, Ila wakes them at dawn and says she dreamed of her father again.
plays.tells: A player asks what happens if they don't go inside.
plays.rules: DC 12 Wisdom saving throw. Mere Memories are borrowed impressions, not losses; record them as 'Mere' in the ledger.
plays.later: Tam's memory is one of the four sources (Eld's papers S3, the Cantor S2, Brannagh Wick). Any two establish the Court's responsibility.
plays.keywords: night, shore, stay, sleep, camp, memory shore, mere memory, dream, wait

plays.title: They row out to find the missing ferry
plays.why: Mother Sallow asks them to; it is the session's clear objective.
plays.readAloud: Below the skiff, rooftops slide past like the backs of sleeping animals. A drowned weathervane points the way you came. Ahead, a ferry sits crooked on a sandbank, and someone is sitting in it.
plays.response: Brannagh Wick lends a skiff and a pilot if asked; without one, the drowned town is a maze of roofs just under the surface. On the sandbank: the ferry, and its dead ferryman, face peaceful, a dripping oar in his hands. That is the Tidewarden's old body; don't name it yet. Memory-eels circle.
plays.consequence: The ferry is found. The eels are between the party and the body.
plays.fallback: If they won't go, the Tidewarden's ferry drifts in to the Old Shore on its own at dawn, its ferryman still holding the oar.
plays.tells: Players ask for a boat, a pilot, or directions to the eastern-marsh route.
plays.rules: Without a pilot: Wisdom (Survival) DC 12 to read the drowned streets. On a failure the skiff scrapes a roof, ships water, and wakes the eels early.
plays.later: S3: the Tidewarden appears to anyone who treated the body with respect, and offers safe passage to the belfry.
plays.keywords: ferry, missing ferry, boat, row, sandbank, skiff, pilot, brannagh, eastern marsh, h-02

plays.title: They fight the memory-eels
plays.why: The eels guard the sandbank and bite anyone who wades.
plays.readAloud: The water around the sandbank thickens into grey ropes, and the ropes have mouths.
plays.response: Run the eel encounter. A bite that deals damage can take a memory; the player chooses which minor memory goes, and it comes back after their next long rest. The eels flee at half their number. Don't add the Drowned Singer to this fight.
plays.consequence: The sandbank is clear. Someone may be missing a small memory until morning.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly, the dead ferryman's oar rises and the eels scatter.
plays.tells: Weapons out at the waterline; someone jumps in.
plays.rules: Encounter: memory-eels. Bite: DC 12 Wisdom save or lose a minor memory until the next long rest (record as 'Eel'). Swimming in the cold Mere: 2024 Frigid Water (minutes equal to Constitution score, then DC 10 Constitution save each minute or 1 Exhaustion level).
plays.later: Level 2 after this first Mere expedition (v5 milestone).
plays.keywords: eels, memory-eels, fight, attack, bite, water, swim, combat, sandbank

plays.title: They slip past the eels
plays.why: Cautious parties avoid a fight in deep water.
plays.readAloud: You drift with the oars up. The grey shapes rise, taste the air above the water, and sink again.
plays.response: Each character in the boat attempts the check. If at least half succeed, the eels never notice and the party reaches the ferry quietly. If not, the eels attack from below with the party in the boat (they can't reach anyone who stays seated for the first round).
plays.consequence: The ferry and body are reached without a fight.
plays.fallback: If the group fails, give the boat one round of grace before the first bite.
plays.tells: Players ask about the eels' behaviour, or ship their oars and drift.
plays.rules: Dexterity (Stealth) DC 13 for each character; succeed as a group if at least half succeed.
plays.later: No eel-thefts to track. The Tidewarden notes their care in S3.
plays.keywords: sneak, stealth, quiet, drift, avoid, eels, slip past

plays.title: They dive to the drowned belfry
plays.why: The bell is visible on calm nights and someone always wants to see it up close (H-07).
plays.readAloud: In the deep water, Old Pellmoor's bell-tower stands like a finger pointing at the sky. Pale figures wait among the arches. One of them turns, and her eyes are too bright.
plays.response: The belfry's top is about forty feet down. The Cantor does not attack unless the party touches the bell. If the Tidewarden has met them kindly, he offers an air pocket around the divers for the length of one conversation. Otherwise, breath and cold are the clock.
plays.consequence: The party meets the Cantor.
plays.fallback: If a diver runs out of air, a drowned hand pushes them gently up to the surface.
plays.tells: A player asks how deep it is, or ties a rope to the skiff.
plays.rules: 2024 Suffocation: hold breath for 1 + Constitution modifier minutes (minimum 30 seconds); out of breath, 1 Exhaustion level at the end of each turn, removed when breathing again. Frigid Water applies to long dives.
plays.later: S2: her question follows. S3: the belfry route is known.
plays.keywords: dive, swim, underwater, belfry, bell, drowned bell, cantor, deep, h-07, breath

plays.title: They answer the Cantor truthfully
plays.why: "Tell me, who are you grieving?" is hard to dodge, and players love a true answer.
plays.readAloud: "You have come down to the bell. Good. Tell me, who are you grieving? Do not lie to me. The dead can tell."
plays.response: The Cantor sings the name back to them, and the water warms. She teaches a verse of Ossa's hymn. If someone sincerely shares a memory of a dead person, she also teaches the full release verse; sharing it here does not erase the memory. Ask her about Ila's father and she says he came to find a safe path to her and never arrived.
plays.consequence: The party knows the release verse. One more source on Tam's death.
plays.fallback: If no one has a loss to name, the Cantor accepts someone grieving on Ila's behalf.
plays.tells: A player names a real loss from their backstory.
plays.rules: The verse grants Advantage on the next saving throw against a Drowned Singer.
plays.later: After Ossa rings, singing the verse releases Ondra and the remaining Choir (S3, or S27). If missed, Mother Sallow can rebuild it from the restored ledger.
plays.keywords: cantor, ondra, grieving, truth, answer, verse, hymn, release, name, dead

plays.title: They lie to the Cantor, or refuse her question
plays.why: Guarded characters won't share grief with a ghost.
plays.readAloud: The Cantor's eyes go dark. The singing stops, and in the silence something long and pale lets go of an arch and comes toward you.
plays.response: One Drowned Singer attacks. The Cantor keeps singing from the water and does not join the fight at this level. The Singer stops pursuit at the surface and treats the response hymn as a ceasefire. Give the divers a clear way up.
plays.consequence: The Choir marks them as the forgetful.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly, the Tidewarden's oar breaks the surface and the Singer withdraws.
plays.tells: A player deflects, jokes, or gives a name they don't mean.
plays.rules: Encounter: one Drowned Singer, underwater. Melee attackers without a Swim Speed have Disadvantage underwater unless using a dagger, javelin, shortsword, spear or trident.
plays.later: S3: the ferry-stair route to the belfry is guarded; they'll need the Tidewarden or the hymn. The Cantor will still bargain if they come back honest.
plays.keywords: lie, refuse, cantor, attack, drowned singer, fight, flee, underwater combat

plays.title: They ask the Cantor about the Tongue
plays.why: The Tongue is the reason anyone is here.
plays.readAloud: "The tongue was taken from us. Ask the ferry-folk what they owe the dead."
plays.response: That is all she says about it. If they brought the Tongue down with them, she goes very still and asks whether they mean to return it. Returning it earns safe access to the bell.
plays.consequence: The party knows the Tongue belongs to the Mere and that the ferry-folk carry a debt.
plays.tells: A player mentions the humming bundle, or brought it with them.
plays.later: S3: Mother Sallow's ledger explains the debt (Tam stole it back from the Court in 392 SS, and the Choir asked for it).
plays.keywords: tongue, ask, cantor, bell, owe, debt, ferry-folk

plays.title: They bring the Tongue down and ring Ossa tonight
plays.why: If the party has the Tongue and reaches the bell, nothing in the rules stops them.
plays.readAloud: The bell rings from under the water. It is deep and slow and it makes the whole Mere ripple. Every grey face on the shore lifts toward the sound. One voice, very old and very clear, speaks a single name.
plays.response: Before anyone fits the Tongue, state the Toll and wait for consent: a memory of someone who has died, chosen by the Ringer. If they say no, the bell does not ring. If they agree, the Drowned fall silent and stop hunting; Mother Sallow, on the shore, suddenly remembers her husband's face and the night of the Wrongweather. The Court will hear of it by the next evening.
plays.consequence: Ossa is rung. The Choir rests. Session 3's Tongue decision is already made.
plays.fallback: If the Toll gives the table pause, let them surface and decide tomorrow; the bell will wait.
plays.tells: The Tongue is in the boat, and a player asks what happens if they fit it.
plays.rules: The Ringer must be at the bell with the Tongue. Record the Toll (kind: Toll, bell: Ossa).
plays.later: S3: run the ledger and Eld; skip the Tongue choice. S4: Maudrin skips her Tongue bargain and is colder. Concord: 1 of 6. With the verse, the Cantor can be released now.
plays.keywords: ring, ossa, bell, toll, early, fit tongue, ring the bell, now

plays.title: They deal with Brother Hadrik's blessing of the Mere
plays.why: A Kelemvorite on Strangers' Row has decided the restless dead are an abomination, and he means to act tonight.
plays.readAloud: "The dead are owed rest, not songs," Brother Hadrik says, uncorking the vial. "Kelemvor's judgment is mercy. Stand aside, or kneel."
plays.response: If Hadrik pours holy water into the Mere during the Night Song and calls on his god, the Choir rises angry and a Drowned Singer comes ashore for him. Talk him down by arguing his own dogma: Kelemvor's dead are meant to be judged and remembered, not erased. Or restrain him; the ferry-folk will thank you, the Court will not care.
plays.consequence: Either the Night Song breaks violently, or Hadrik becomes a reluctant friend.
plays.fallback: If the party ignores him, Mother Sallow intervenes and gets hurt; the Old Shore blames the Loud Quarter.
plays.tells: Players notice a grey-robed foreigner with a censer and a vial of holy water heading for the Memory Shore.
plays.rules: Influence, Charisma (Persuasion) DC 15; he's Indifferent. A successful DC 12 Intelligence (Religion) Study check about Kelemvor's teachings first grants Advantage.
plays.later: If he succeeds: the Choir hunts harder (S3 belfry guarded by two Singers). If persuaded: he blesses the Ringer before Ossa rings and can be an ally in Pellmoor later.
plays.keywords: hadrik, kelemvor, priest, holy water, bless, exorcise, turn undead, foreigner, censer

plays.title: They ask the Pilots' Hall about Tam Harrow
plays.why: Tam was a pilot; his colleagues know things the family doesn't.
plays.readAloud: Brannagh Wick coils her sounding-line slowly, twice, before she answers. "Tam took her out the night he died. No cargo. No ship to bring in. No pilot does that, lad. Not unless he's going somewhere he can't write down."
plays.response: Brannagh told the Landing House nothing. She thinks Tam was going to the drowned belfry, and she's right. She'll say so if Ila vouches for the party or if they've helped the ferry-folk.
plays.consequence: One more source on Tam's death.
plays.tells: Players ask who Tam worked with, or where he took his boat.
plays.rules: Influence, Charisma (Persuasion) DC 15; automatic success if Ila vouches for them or they filled the quota.
plays.later: S3: with any second source (Eld's patrol entry, the Cantor, a Mere Memory of Tam) the Court's responsibility is established. Brannagh can also delay any ship from leaving the Mere: no pilot, no departure.
plays.keywords: brannagh, pilots hall, pilot, tam, harrow, father, boat, how he died, investigate

edits.find: - The ferry for the eastern marsh has not returned. Mother Sallow asks the party to find it.
edits.replace: - The ferry for the eastern marsh has not returned. Mother Sallow asks the party to find it. Pilot-Mistress Brannagh Wick lends a skiff and a pilot; without one, the drowned rooftops just under the surface make the crossing a maze (DC 12 Wisdom (Survival)).

edits.find: - In the deep water, Old Pellmoor's Ossa Belfry stands like a finger.
edits.replace: - In the deep water, Old Pellmoor's Ossa Belfry stands like a finger, its top about forty feet down. Use the 2024 Suffocation rules (hold breath for 1 + Constitution modifier minutes) unless the Tidewarden grants an air pocket.

edits.find: **Session 2 end:**
edits.replace:
**Complication (v6, optional): Brother Hadrik Voss.** A Kelemvorite priest from Strangers' Row means to "lay the dead to rest" by blessing the Mere during the Night Song. sessions.summary: The Night Song, a missing ferry on a sandbank, memory-eels, and a question from the deep: who are you grieving?

plays.title: They search Brother Eld's desk
plays.why: Mother Sallow names him, and the page has to be somewhere.
plays.readAloud: The desk is very neat. Too neat. The drawer that sticks has been oiled.
plays.response: Once they have access, the page is found without a roll. A good search also turns up the matching Court forms and a recent patrol entry recording Tam Harrow's interrogation. Failure only costs time and brings Eld in from the vestry, frightened.
plays.consequence: The party holds the missing page, with Ila's name on it.
plays.fallback: If they won't search, Eld brings them the page himself the next morning, unable to sleep.
plays.tells: Players ask when the chapel is empty, or how to get Eld out of it.
plays.rules: Study action, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 14 finds it quickly, with the forms and the patrol entry. The essential clue is never lost to a failed check.
plays.later: The patrol entry is a source on Tam's death. S4: if they took the forms, Rook (S6) values them as evidence.
plays.keywords: eld, desk, search, chapel, page, ledger, find, investigate, steal, forms

plays.title: They confront Eld privately and take the page
plays.why: A quiet confrontation protects the children and lets Eld save face.
plays.readAloud: "The page is in my desk, Mother. The Court asked me to keep it. I didn't read it, because I didn't want to. But I know what it says. I copied the names onto the Court's forms myself."
plays.response: Eld asks for absolution before anything else. He gives them the name of one child on the list whose family can still be warned, and then he leaves Pellmoor on the next ferry.
plays.consequence: Eld is gone. One family is warned in time.
plays.tells: Players wait until Eld is alone.
plays.later: S4: Eld is not at the Assembly; use an unnamed Court chaplain.
plays.keywords: confront, eld, private, page, absolution, forgive, leave

plays.title: They expose Eld in front of the village
plays.why: The page names children. Some parties want justice in public.
plays.readAloud: Nobody shouts. That is the worst of it. The ferry-folk just look at him, one family at a time, until he can't stand it.
plays.response: The village turns on him. Eld flees to Hallowmere that night in shame and becomes a Court chaplain. Mother Sallow says nothing kind and nothing cruel.
plays.consequence: Eld is in Hallowmere, humiliated and useful to the Court.
plays.tells: Players gather the Old Shore, or read names aloud at the chapel door.
plays.later: S4: Eld is at the Assembly as a Court chaplain and will not meet their eyes. The Court learns what the party knows about the page.
plays.keywords: expose, public, accuse, shame, eld, village, crowd, justice

plays.title: They forgive Eld
plays.why: Eld is pliant, sorry, and offers help; mercy is a real option.
plays.readAloud: Eld cries like a man who has been holding it in for two years. When he stops, he asks what he can do, and he means it.
plays.response: He becomes the party's informant in Act II: he still writes to the Court, and now he tells the party what he writes. His loyalty depends on how they protect him and the children. Foreshadow any renewed Court pressure before he wavers.
plays.consequence: The party has a source inside the Church.
plays.tells: A cleric or a kind character responds to his request for absolution.
plays.later: S4: Eld meets their eyes at the Assembly and slips them a note about Haldric's armory. S6: he can testify at the oath-duel if protected.
plays.keywords: forgive, absolve, mercy, eld, informant, redemption, spare

plays.title: They tell Ila the truth about her name on the list
plays.why: Ila recognises her own name and begins to cry; someone will speak to her.
plays.readAloud: Ila reads her own name twice. Then she says, very quietly, "That's why he was scared. Not of the water. Of them."
plays.response: Ila trusts people who tell her the truth about hard things. If they explain what the list means, she asks to decide the Tongue's fate with them, and asks whether she can come. If they say "don't worry about it," she stops talking to that character.
plays.consequence: Ila's trust is earned or lost here.
plays.tells: A player turns to Ila instead of Eld.
plays.later: S3 Tongue choice: she argues for returning it to the Mere. Taking her along keeps her close and in danger; hiding her with the Pilots' Hall keeps her safe.
plays.keywords: ila, comfort, truth, list, name, cry, tell her, father

plays.title: They work out how Tam Harrow died
plays.why: By now the party likely holds two of the four sources.
plays.readAloud: It isn't a mystery anymore. It's a ferry with no cargo, a patrol in grey gloves, and a man who couldn't remember the way home.
plays.response: Confirm it when any two sources agree: a Court patrol took Tam's memory of the route to the belfry and left him on the water; he fell in and drowned; the Choir kept his body, but did not kill him. Let Ila hear it from whoever she trusts most.
plays.consequence: The Court is responsible for Tam's death, and the party knows it.
plays.fallback: If they have only one source, Mother Sallow supplies the second from the ledger: Tam's name, with a Court mark beside it.
plays.tells: Players line up the patrol entry, the Cantor's words, Brannagh's story, or a Mere Memory.
plays.later: S6: Wren's confession (she gave the Court Tam's name) lands hard. Ila's anger shapes her choices for the rest of the campaign.
plays.keywords: tam, death, murder, how he died, clues, solve, patrol, route, memory taken

plays.title: They return the Tongue to the Mere
plays.why: Ila, Mother Sallow and the Cantor all point this way.
plays.readAloud: The Tidewarden is waiting at the end of the old dock, oar dripping. He doesn't ask where you're going.
plays.response: The ferry-stair is safest, and the Choir guards it. The Tidewarden holds a pocket of breathable air around anyone who accepts peaceful passage; Mother Sallow's hymn earns that passage without any memory price. Diving magic or a sound alternative plan also works. At the belfry, the Cantor asks whether they mean to ring it.
plays.consequence: The Tongue is home. The Drowned stop hunting Pellmoor while it stays there.
plays.fallback: If they hesitate at the water's edge, Ila takes the bundle and steps into the Tidewarden's ferry herself.
plays.tells: Players ask how to reach the drowned belfry safely.
plays.rules: If not using the Tidewarden: 2024 Suffocation and Frigid Water apply.
plays.later: Ringing is a separate choice with a Toll (next play). The Court still wants the Tongue (S4).
plays.keywords: return, give back, mere, belfry, tidewarden, choir, cantor, put back

plays.title: They ring Ossa
plays.why: With the Tongue at the bell, the question is only who pays.
plays.readAloud: The bell rings from under the water. It is deep and slow and it makes the whole Mere ripple. Every grey face on the shore lifts toward the sound. The Drowned fall silent, and one voice, very old and very clear, speaks a single name. Then the Mere is only water again, and the reeds bend in a breeze that smells of rain.
plays.response: State the Toll first and wait for a yes: a memory of someone who has died, chosen by the Ringer. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. If they ring it, the Choir rests, and Mother Sallow remembers her husband Davin and the night of the Wrongweather. If anyone sings the Cantor's release verse afterward, Ondra speaks her own name and goes quiet.
plays.consequence: Ossa is rung. The dead of the Mere may rest.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer is unsure, the Cantor waits. A bell that waited four hundred years can wait a night.
plays.tells: A player asks what ringing would do, or what it costs.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (kind: Toll, bell: Ossa). The deceased person need not be a loved one (v5 2.11).
plays.later: Concord: 1 of 6. S4: no Tongue bargain at the Assembly. The Court withdraws collectors from the newly quiet Mere for a while (Court clock +1). S27: the Choir can sing at the summit if released.
plays.keywords: ring, ossa, toll, bell, ring the bell, memory of the dead, ringer

plays.title: They sing the Cantor's release verse after Ossa rings
plays.why: If they learned the verse in Session 2, this is the moment it was for.
plays.readAloud: The verse is short. When it ends, the Cantor sings her own name, Ondra Sallow, in a voice nobody has heard for two hundred and sixty years. Then she goes quiet, and so does everyone else under the water.
plays.response: The singer must sincerely commemorate a dead person. Ondra and the remaining Choir are released. Released spirits may return once, willingly, as allies; they are never compelled back.
plays.consequence: The Drowned Choir is released.
plays.tells: A player asks whether the Choir can be freed now.
plays.later: S22/S27: the Cantor may return once as an ally. S28: Mother Sallow sings the last verse with Ila.
plays.keywords: release, verse, sing, cantor, ondra, free the choir, choir, rest

plays.title: They carry the Tongue to Hallowmere
plays.why: Some parties want allies (the Dawn Order, the Bellwrights) before deciding.
plays.readAloud: The bundle hums all the way to the edge of the Mere road, and then, as the reeds give way to grey hedges, it goes quiet, as if it knows where it's going.
plays.response: Act II begins early. Brannagh can ferry them across the Mere (three days to the capital instead of six) and knows a landing that skips the first checkpoint. Faerûnians still need the Chancellor's invitation or a writ.
plays.consequence: The party is on the road to Hallowmere with Ossa's Tongue.
plays.tells: Players ask who in the capital opposes the Court.
plays.later: S4: the Gate Clerk already has their names (+2 to Persuasion DCs). Maudrin's bargain targets the Tongue they carry. Concord: Ossa still needs a return to the Mere (the Tidewarden ferries the Ringer once they hold it again).
plays.keywords: hallowmere, capital, carry, take it, dawn order, bellwrights, travel, leave pellmoor, road

plays.title: They keep the Tongue in Pellmoor and defend the village
plays.why: A protective party won't let the Court take anything from the Old Shore.
plays.readAloud: Quill comes back with every Hushman the Landing House has, and a written deadline nailed to the chapel door. Behind him, forty foreign masts stand very still on the water and do nothing at all.
plays.response: Act II begins as a siege. Quill issues a deadline; villagers prepare shelter and an evacuation route; the party negotiates, resists a patrol, or leads an escape. The foreign ships stay neutral, but Brannagh can close the Mere to Court boats: no pilot, no crossing. Intercepted orders point to the Hallowmere vault.
plays.consequence: Pellmoor is under Court pressure and will be changed by it.
plays.fallback: If the siege drags, the Pilots' Hall offers to smuggle the Tongue out by night.
plays.tells: Players ask about defences, the Landing House's strength, or who would fight.
plays.rules: Use the Hushmen Line (Act II) scaled for level 3. Show retreat routes and the deadline before any fighting.
plays.later: S4: a short siege outline replaces the gate scene; the intercepted orders lead to Hallowmere. The Old Shore's trust is earned for the rest of the campaign. Faerûnian traders note which side the party took.
plays.keywords: keep, defend, protect, siege, stay, fight the court, village, pellmoor, barricade

plays.title: They send the Tongue to the Chancellor
plays.why: Greedy or desperate parties take the Court's reward.
plays.readAloud: The order comes back with the receipt, sealed in the same grey wax: the arrest of one Ila Harrow, listener, for questioning.
plays.response: Show the arrest order to the players before anyone acts on it. Give them a chance to warn, hide, or escort Ila. If the arrest succeeds, her rescue in Hallowmere becomes an Act II objective.
plays.consequence: The Court holds the Tongue and wants Ila.
plays.tells: Players ask what the Court would pay, or want to end the danger quickly.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin is delighted and offers Ila's Tithe-exemption instead of a bargain. If Ila is taken, she is held in the Hall of Tithes (rescue alongside Tessa in S6). Concord: Ossa needs the Tongue recovered.
plays.keywords: give, maudrin, court, chancellor, sell to the court, reward, surrender

plays.title: They sell the Tongue to Master Venn
plays.why: A Faerûnian buyer offers real gold and a way out of Corvane's problems.
plays.readAloud: Venn counts the gold onto the table himself, coin by coin, smiling. "The Gilded Heron sails in three days. Your relic will be admired in Athkatla by people who have never heard of a Toll. Isn't that a kindness?"
plays.response: Venn pays 600 gp (Influence, Persuasion, DC 15 raises it to 900; his buyer pays 5,000). The Tongue goes aboard the Gilded Heron, which needs a pilot to leave the Mere and a day to cross the Seam. Ila learns within the hour. Brannagh Wick can delay the ship one day by refusing a pilot.
plays.consequence: The Tongue is on a foreign ship. The clock is three days, maybe four.
plays.fallback: If the players regret it, Venn will sell it back for 1,200 gp or a heartkeep, and enjoy the profit.
plays.tells: Players ask what Venn would pay, or whether selling abroad keeps it from the Court.
plays.rules: Record the sale. The Heron leaves in 3 days; Brannagh can add 1; the Seam crossing takes 1 more.
plays.later: If it clears the Seam: Ossa can't be rung and Concord is impossible until it is recovered (safety valve if the table wants it: the Heron wrecks in the Stormwall and the Tongue washes back into the Mere weeks later). S4: the Court is furious with Venn, and with the party. S28: Ila never forgives it.
plays.keywords: sell, venn, merchant, gold, coster, gilded heron, ship, abroad, athkatla, profit, buyer

plays.title: They try to get the Tongue back from the Gilded Heron
plays.why: If the Tongue was sold, regret (or Ila) arrives quickly.
plays.readAloud: The Gilded Heron rides at anchor beyond the last pier, lamps lit, a drowned church spire just under her keel.
plays.response: Three ways: board her at night past two Coster guards; persuade Brannagh to deny her a pilot until Venn deals; or buy it back (1,200 gp or a heartkeep). Venn prefers money to trouble and folds once a guard drops or the Pilots' Hall turns against him.
plays.consequence: The Tongue is recovered, or it sails.
plays.fallback: If they fail, the Heron's first mate, a Baldurian who toasts the Gull's Wager, offers to 'lose' it overboard for 100 gp.
plays.tells: Players ask where the Heron is anchored, or who pilots her out.
plays.rules: Boarding: Dexterity (Stealth) DC 13 per character, or the encounter. Venn is Indifferent; he becomes Hostile only if humiliated in public.
plays.later: Recovered: Venn holds a grudge and pays Quill to watch the party (S4 Court knows them). Lost: see 'They sell the Tongue to Master Venn'.
plays.keywords: recover, steal back, board, ship, gilded heron, venn, buy back, pilot, retrieve

plays.title: They accept the Chancellor's invitation
plays.why: The letter arrives whatever they chose, and it promises safety and answers.
plays.readAloud: "To those who carried the Tongue of Ossa from Pellmoor: the Quiet Court extends its gratitude and its invitation. The Chancellor would be honoured by your presence at the Quiet Assembly in Hallowmere, in ten days. You will be safe. You will be remembered. Nothing you carry will be asked of you that you do not wish to give. M. Vesk, Quiet Chancellor, Warden of Silence."
plays.response: The grey seal makes the letter a writ of passage for everyone named in it, Stormborn included. Brannagh offers the Mere crossing. Level up to 3 when the Tongue decision is resolved.
plays.consequence: The party is expected at the Quiet Assembly.
plays.tells: Players read the letter twice, or ask whether it's a trap.
plays.later: S4: the gate accepts the letter as a writ. Maudrin has read Quill's report and knows their faces.
plays.keywords: invitation, letter, assembly, accept, go, hallowmere, writ, chancellor

plays.title: They refuse the invitation
plays.why: A letter from the people who killed Tam is easy to burn.
plays.readAloud: The letter curls in the fire. The grey wax doesn't melt. It sits in the ashes, perfectly round, until someone picks it up.
plays.response: Don't force the trip. Captain Rook or Wren Caddock brings the investigation to them instead (a Dawn Order rider, or a Bellwright courier asking for help). The wax seal still works as a writ if they keep it.
plays.consequence: The Court takes note of the refusal.
plays.tells: Players call it a trap, or burn it.
plays.later: S4: start with Rook's or Wren's request instead of the Assembly; Maudrin's bargain comes later, by letter. The Court's clock ticks.
plays.keywords: refuse, burn, decline, ignore, trap, invitation, letter, no

sessions.summary: A missing ledger page, a frightened friar, and the choice of what to do with the Tongue before the Court decides for you.

plays.title: They give the courtesy memory at the gate
plays.why: It is presented as a formality, the clerk is pitiable, and refusing looks like trouble on the first day.
plays.readAloud: The clerk touches a tuning fork to a vial of grey glass and holds it near your temple. It feels like forgetting a word you were about to say, and then not minding. He writes your name in the book without looking up. “Welcome to Hallowmere. You won't miss it.”
plays.response: Each player chooses the memory and writes one line in the Memory Ledger; you never choose it. Log it as a Tithe, not a Toll: it sits in a labelled jar in the Tithe-Ledger Room and its owner can redeem it by opening the jar. Clerk Oswin Tell is a Blank; asked why he works here, he says “Someone must,” and looks frightened that he cannot say who. If anyone offers gold he stares at the coin as if it were a pebble: the courtesy memory is a registration, not a fee, and the Hallowmere gate takes no gold for it.
plays.consequence: The party is in the Tithe-system. Any Hushman can look up their names and what they gave.
plays.fallback: If a player can't pick, offer a mote: last Ossday's supper, a stranger's coat, the second verse of a song.
plays.tells: Players ask “What happens to it?” or start choosing something small.
plays.rules: No check. Record as a Tithe (redeemable), not a Toll. A Reckoner's draw takes about a minute and needs consent.
plays.later: S5: each courtesy jar sits on the vault's newest shelf, near the character's older earliest-memory jar. S7 and S9: Hushmen at the line and the north gate know their names on sight.
plays.keywords: gate, courtesy memory, register, registration, tithe, clerk, give memory, entry, gold, pay, oswin

plays.title: They refuse the courtesy memory
plays.why: Players who spent three sessions learning what the Tithe costs will balk at feeding it.
plays.readAloud: The clerk's pen stops. He looks past you, at the two grey-gloved men by the arch, and says in a small voice, “Sergeant? These ones won't.”
plays.response: Refusing needs Influence (Persuasion) DC 15 on Sergeant Mabry Cole, or a bribe: Cole takes 10 gp a head, Tithes a mote of his own to fill the line, and pockets the gold. If that fails, Cole calls his men (Gate Hushmen). The party can run into the lamp-lit lanes (DC 13 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) each) or talk their way out (DC 15 Charisma (Deception): 'the Chancellor promised us exemption'). Anyone who fails spends a day and a night in a cell in Vaer's Belfry, and Captain Rook hears of it by evening and visits the cell herself.
plays.consequence: The party stays outside the Tithe-system, and the gate remembers their faces as refusers.
plays.fallback: If it bogs down, the Assembly's carriage arrives for 'the Chancellor's guests' and Cole steps back, furious.
plays.tells: A flat “No,” or a player asks what happens if they don't.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Cole's Intelligence is 14). Athletics or Acrobatics DC 13 to flee; Deception DC 15. Add +2 to these DCs if the party carried the Tongue to Hallowmere early in S3. A night in the Belfry is a night in a Court city (Tithe Clock +1).
plays.later: S6: a jailed character meets Rook early; she opens the commission in the cell. S9: Cole is on the north gate on the day they leave and remembers refusers (+2 to any bluff there).
plays.keywords: refuse, no, won't give, bribe guard, run, flee, gate, hushmen, deception, belfry, jail, cell, cole, sergeant

plays.title: A Stormborn character shows their papers
plays.why: Under the Landing Charter, Faerûnians need a writ of passage beyond the Mere road, and the Hallowmere gate checks.
plays.readAloud: Sergeant Cole holds the grey-sealed letter to the lamp and reads the signature twice. Then he hands it back very carefully, as if it might bruise. “Guests of the Assembly. Loudfolk too, it seems.”
plays.response: The Chancellor's invitation counts as a writ for everyone it names, Stormborn included. A forged writ gets past the Blank clerk but not Cole, who checks the grey wax (DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation)); a failed forgery is arrest for 'landing past the Charter' unless they talk or run as above. With no writ at all, a Faerûnian is turned back to the Mere road; a Corvane Venture cloth wagon gets them in by night (DC 14 Dexterity (Stealth)). Inland, nobody speaks Common: Faerûnians without Hesk need a companion to translate, or Comprehend Languages or Tongues.
plays.consequence: Stormborn characters are inside Hallowmere, lawfully or not. Hushmen stare at dragonborn, tieflings and gnomes, and whisper that aasimar are bell-touched.
plays.fallback: If a player feels locked out, a palace clerk arrives with a fresh writ 'for the Chancellor's guests', which also shows how closely Maudrin watches them.
plays.tells: A Sword Coast character produces papers, or asks whether foreigners are allowed in.
plays.rules: Investigation DC 15 (Cole vs a forgery). Stealth DC 14 to ride in under cloth. Comprehend Languages or Tongues for Hesk.
plays.later: S9: a forged-writ character is stopped at the north gate unless they leave under Rook's escort or a smuggling route. Act IV: if Thrane rings, the Charter collapses and writs stop mattering.
plays.keywords: writ, passage, papers, faerunian, stormborn, loudfolk, foreigner, forged, seal, grey wax, charter, hesk, language, tongues, translate

plays.title: They bring Sister Aurelie into the city
plays.why: The Court has refused Aurelie's writ four times; a party with the Chancellor's invitation looks like her chance.
plays.readAloud: Sister Aurelie lowers her hood at the edge of the marsh road and looks up at the grey disc of the sun. “When the sun comes back,” she says, “I'd like to be standing somewhere it can see me.”
plays.response: The invitation does not name her. Passing her off as the party's scribe is Influence (Deception) DC 15 against Cole; hiding her in a cart is DC 14 Dexterity (Stealth) for her, with advantage if someone Helps. Inside, she cannot stay quiet: within two days she wants to sing a dawn-hymn on the Terraces of Grief. If caught, she is held in Vaer's Belfry as a Charter-breaker, unharmed, and the Court will offer to trade her for something the party has.
plays.consequence: Aurelie is in Hallowmere: a healer, an ally, and a liability.
plays.fallback: If smuggling her stalls, she gives the party a letter for 'the Dawn Mission's first friend in Hallowmere' and goes back to Pellmoor to wait.
plays.tells: The party met Aurelie on Strangers' Row, or a cleric or paladin of Lathander asks about the Dawn Mission.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Cole). Stealth DC 14; Help gives advantage. Aurelie uses Priest stats (Healing Word, Lesser Restoration, Dispel Magic).
plays.later: S9: if Vaer rings while she is in the city, she becomes devoted to the party, and is arrested by dusk unless someone gets her out. S22: a free Aurelie is the core of the Stormborn ally.
plays.keywords: aurelie, dawnmantle, lathander, dawn mission, morninglord, smuggle, sneak in, cart, cleric, priest, disguise

plays.title: They stayed to defend Pellmoor
plays.why: A party that kept the Tongue in Pellmoor (S3) opens Act II under siege instead of at the gate.
plays.readAloud: The notice is nailed to the chapel door in Quill's neat hand: 'By the Office of Tithes. Surrender all unlicensed bell-work by Hushday dusk. Thereafter the Old Shore will be searched house by house.'
plays.response: Run it short: Quill gives three days. The villagers want a shelter (the ledger-house) and an escape route (Brannagh Wick's pilots can take the Old Shore across the Mere in two nights). The party negotiates, resists one patrol (Siege Patrol), or leads the evacuation. Whatever happens, the patrol's Sergeant carries orders in grey wax: 'Ossa relic to the Tithe-Ledger Room, Hallowmere, by Vaerday.' The party chooses whether to follow them; the marsh road out is cordoned (DC 14 Dexterity (Stealth) as a group).
plays.consequence: Pellmoor is changed either way: the Old Shore is evacuated, or it stood, and the Court remembers. Set Pellmoor to 'Changed' or 'Old Shore evacuated'.
plays.fallback: If the siege drags, Quill accepts a parley: one memory 'for the quota' from a volunteer, and he withdraws for a week.
plays.tells: The Tongue is still in Pellmoor and Quill's notice is on the chapel door.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 14 past the cordon; Pass without Trace gives +10. Influence DC 15 on Quill (Indifferent, Hostile if the party is a Tithe-case).
plays.later: S9: the party can come back to Pellmoor instead of going north. S22: defended ferry-folk keep Court ships on the Mere for a day (no pilot, no departure). S28: 'Who keeps the ledger now?' depends on who stayed.
plays.keywords: siege, defend pellmoor, quill, deadline, evacuate, cordon, marsh road, patrol, orders, old shore, stay

plays.title: They refuse the invitation or never go to the Assembly
plays.why: Some tables smell a trap and stay away from the Chancellor entirely.
plays.readAloud: A broad woman in a dawn-coloured cloak gone grey sits down across from you without asking and sets a Dawn Order seal on the table. “You turned down the Chancellor. Good. Then you might be the only people in this city who'll listen to me.”
plays.response: Bring the investigation to them. Captain Dessa Rook finds them at their lodgings and opens her commission early (S6, Scene 1); or Wren Caddock, sewing on a bench outside the Bone Archive, asks too many friendly questions and mentions that Lysse Carrow 'needs someone brave'. Maudrin is not offended: she sends a single grey rose to their lodgings with no note, and two Hushmen follow them for the rest of the Act.
plays.consequence: No bargain is offered, so no favor is owed. The Court watches them closely.
plays.fallback: If they wander, Lysse Carrow drops a bone-bound book at their feet in the street and asks them to carry it back to the Archive.
plays.tells: “We're not going to her party.” Or they head straight for the Bone Archive or the Dawn Order.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 13 to shake the Hushmen for a day.
plays.later: S8: Maudrin's last word still comes, through Isolde. S23: with no favor owed, Maudrin runs the Strike normally.
plays.keywords: refuse invitation, skip assembly, don't go, avoid maudrin, stay away, rook, wren, investigation, lysse

plays.title: They accept Maudrin's bargain for Ossa's Tongue
plays.why: Safe passage, a pension and a protected memory are a real offer, and some players are tired of being hunted.
plays.readAloud: “Safe passage. A Court pension. And one memory of your choosing that no Tithe will ever touch.” Maudrin folds her grey gloves. “All I ask is the thing your friend is carrying, which was never yours to carry.”
plays.response: Maudrin keeps her word about exactly what she promised. Each character names one memory on a grey card she signs: no Court Tithe can take it (Tolls, the stairs of the Hush and eel bites are not Tithes). She calls Ser Haldric, who carries the Tongue to the Dawn Order armory beside Vaer's Tongue, so the party sees a Dawn Order knight take the Chancellor's orders. The pension is 5 gp a month for Stormborn (she knows they prefer gold) or 5 keeps for Corvanese.
plays.consequence: Ossa's Tongue is in the Dawn Order armory. The party owes Maudrin one favor.
plays.fallback: If the table splits, Maudrin gives them until the end of the masque and dances with Isolde while they argue.
plays.tells: A player asks exactly what the exemption covers, or looks at the bundle and then at the others.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 (Maudrin's Intelligence) to haggle a better term, such as Ila's exemption too. Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.later: S6: if Rook wins the hearing, she takes the armory and hands Ossa's Tongue back to the party. S9: or they steal it with Vaer's (DC 15 Thieves' Tools). S23: Maudrin calls the favor in on the ridge: “One favor, dear, and I am calling it in now. Go, before I change my mind.”
plays.keywords: accept, bargain, deal, maudrin, exemption, pension, safe passage, hand over, give tongue, favor, ossa

plays.title: They refuse Maudrin's bargain
plays.why: Most tables have decided by now that the Court is the problem.
plays.readAloud: Her smile does not move at all. “Then the Assembly will go on without you. Enjoy the city.”
plays.response: She does not threaten. Two Hushmen follow the party for the rest of the Act at a polite distance; a DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth) group check loses them for a day, and they are back next morning. Isolde Drave finds the party within the hour, delighted: people who refuse Maudrin are the most interesting people in the room. For one true story about the Mere, Isolde trades one true secret: 'The Tithe-Ledger Room has a service passage, and a Hushman named Ilam Bray walks past it every evening.'
plays.consequence: No favor is owed. The Court watches them, and Isolde is curious.
plays.fallback: If they freeze, Maudrin answers the question nobody asked: 'Yes, I know about your Tongue. Everyone does.'
plays.tells: Players answer with a question about the Tithe, or say no outright.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 13 to shake the tail (once a day). Isolde: Influence DC 15, Indifferent; clever talk makes her Friendly. Record in the Bargain Log: refused.
plays.later: S7: the Ilam Bray lead pays off. S8: Maudrin's last word is warmer than they expect. S15: Isolde already knows their habits. S23: with no favor owed, Maudrin runs the Strike normally.
plays.keywords: refuse, no deal, decline, reject bargain, maudrin, hushmen follow, tail, isolde, gossip

plays.title: They tell Maudrin where the Tongue is
plays.why: The party no longer carries Ossa's Tongue, so Maudrin changes the bargain: “Then tell me where it is, and you will be rewarded.”
plays.readAloud: “Then you don't have it.” Maudrin smiles as if you have passed a test. “Tell me where it is, and you will be rewarded. Lie to me and I'll know by morning, which would be a waste of both our evenings.”
plays.response: She wants a place, not a promise, and the truth costs whoever holds it. With Ila: Hushmen ride for Pellmoor within a day, and the party has two days to warn her. In the Dawn Order armory: Maudrin already knew and only wanted to see if they would say it. On Venn's Gilded Heron or gone through the Seam: the Court seizes Venn's cargo at the Landing House, and Venn learns who told. Telling her earns the pension and exemption, and the favor.
plays.consequence: The party owes Maudrin a favor, and whoever holds the Tongue is in danger.
plays.fallback: If they won't say, play s04-bargain-refuse.
plays.tells: The Tongue is with Ila, the Dawn Order, the Bellwrights, or Master Venn, and a player starts weighing the pension.
plays.rules: Deception against Maudrin's Insight (+4); anything the Court's records contradict fails automatically. Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.later: S23: the favor is called in on the ridge. If they named Ila, she can be arrested before S6 and held in the Hall of Tithes (rescue alongside Tessa). If they named Venn, he treats them as enemies on their return to Pellmoor.
plays.keywords: tell, reveal, where is it, location, inform, maudrin, ila, venn, dawn order, armory, reward

plays.title: They take Maudrin's exemption for Ila
plays.why: Maudrin already holds Ossa's Tongue (S3), so she bargains for the girl who heard it.
plays.readAloud: “I have the Tongue. You were very sensible.” Maudrin turns her glass in her fingers. “The girl who heard it, though. Ila. My office has an order for her. I could lose it, and give her the same exemption I'd give you. For a favor.”
plays.response: This is the only bargain she has to offer. If Ila was arrested after S3, Maudrin offers her release to Pellmoor with the exemption: set Ila to 'Free in Pellmoor'. If Ila is free, Maudrin tears the arrest order in half in front of them. Either way, the party owes the favor. If they refuse, the order stands and Hushmen move on Ila within two days.
plays.consequence: Ila is safe from the Court's Tithe for now. The party owes Maudrin a favor.
plays.fallback: If the party argues morality with her, she agrees with every word and keeps the order in her hand.
plays.tells: Players ask about Ila, or whether the arrest order can be withdrawn.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 to add anything to the deal. Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.later: S23: the favor is called in, and Maudrin reminds them who it was for. S28: Ila, untithed, grows up to keep the ledger and to ring the ferry-folk's bell.
plays.keywords: ila, exemption, arrest order, release, protect ila, maudrin, favor, bargain, child

plays.title: Ossa's Tongue went back to the Mere
plays.why: The Tongue is at the Ossa Belfry (S3), so there is nothing to bargain for, and Maudrin knows it.
plays.readAloud: “You put it back.” Maudrin says it gently, as if she were sorry for them. “Every glass in my palace hummed that night. I had them all wrapped in cloth.”
plays.response: Skip the bargain. She asks, with real curiosity, what the bell sounded like, and listens to the answer. She offers one smaller deal from Part 9: a Court pension in exchange for their silence about what they found under the Mere; accepting it means they owe her the favor. If Ossa was rung, she says the Court will 'revisit Pellmoor's quota in the spring', which means the collectors have withdrawn for now.
plays.consequence: No Tongue changes hands. Maudrin has measured them.
plays.fallback: If the table wants a fight with her, she introduces them to Isolde and leaves.
plays.tells: Maudrin greets them without asking for anything.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 if they want anything else from her. Insight DC 15: she is relieved the Tongue is not in the city.
plays.later: S23: a favor is owed only if they took the pension. Act V: Ossa's resonance persists for the Concord whatever the Court does to Pellmoor.
plays.keywords: returned, belfry, mere, ossa rung, no tongue, assembly, pension, silence, maudrin

plays.title: They find Brother Eld among the guests
plays.why: An exposed or forgiven Eld came to Hallowmere and serves as a Court chaplain at the masque.
plays.readAloud: A tall, round-shouldered man in chaplain's grey stands by the punch with his mask slightly crooked. Ink still on his fingers. He sees you, and his face does the sad thing it was trained to do.
plays.response: If Eld fled in disgrace, he will not meet their eyes; cornered behind a pillar, he begs them not to tell anyone what he did, and buys their silence with the name of the Court's new Pellmoor informer, a ferry-boy called Coll who owes the Landing House money. If they forgave him, he meets their eyes and slips a folded hymn-sheet into a pocket as he passes: 'Your names came up the river in Quill's report. Ser Haldric carried it to the palace, not to the Order.'
plays.consequence: The party has an informant (forgiven) or a frightened man who owes them his secret (fled).
plays.fallback: If they ignore him, a forgiven Eld finds them at the door with the same note; a disgraced one avoids them all night.
plays.tells: A player scans the room for familiar faces, or asks who the chaplain is.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15: Friendly if forgiven, Hostile with fear if exposed. Intimidation works on a frightened Eld and sends him running to Haldric.
plays.later: S6: Eld's note is a corroborating witness that Haldric serves the palace, though not proof of payment. S28: Eld confesses publicly, dies in the Mere, or leaves forever, following how they treat him now.
plays.keywords: eld, brother eld, chaplain, priest, informant, ledger page, pellmoor, mask, note, haldric

plays.title: They threaten Maudrin at the masque
plays.why: A frustrated or bold player decides the villain is right there and lightly guarded.
plays.readAloud: She laughs, softly, delighted. “Oh, you're adorable. Haldric, please see to our guests.”
plays.response: Ser Haldric Mose arrives with four palace guards: a Dawn Order knight answering the Chancellor's call is the surprise. He asks them to leave, courteously, twice. If they fight, use Haldric's Escort; Maudrin leaves by a side door and casts only if someone casts at her (Counterspell). Nobody dies at the masque: guests scream, guards grapple, and anyone dropped wakes in Vaer's Belfry.
plays.consequence: The party is a named enemy, and they have seen Haldric take the Chancellor's orders.
plays.fallback: If it starts to go badly, Isolde steps between them with a fresh glass and a joke, and the guards take the hint.
plays.tells: Hands on hilts, a raised voice, a spell component in a fist.
plays.rules: Haldric's silence-stone shield negates the first spell that targets only him each day. Maudrin: Counterspell (3/day). Grappled, Prone. A knock-out is the default for every Court combatant.
plays.later: S6: 'Who called you to the masque, Ser Haldric?' is a fair question on the Dawn Steps, though not proof of payment. S23: Maudrin remembers this evening when she makes her offer on the ridge.
plays.keywords: threaten, attack maudrin, kill, assassinate, fight, masque, haldric, guards, violence, intimidate

plays.title: They mention a key that can ring the Seventh
plays.why: Players who picked up rumours from Eld's papers, a Mere Memory or a Bellwright may test Maudrin with it.
plays.readAloud: Her face goes still for half a second, the way the Mere goes still. Then she says, quite pleasantly, “I have no idea what you mean,” and turns to thank the musicians.
plays.response: The Assembly ends early: the music stops, Hushmen open the doors, and guests are thanked for coming. Maudrin does not look at the party again tonight. By the time they reach their lodgings, two Hushmen stand at the door and their Tithe records are flagged.
plays.consequence: The party is the Court's enemy.
plays.fallback: If nobody pushes further, Isolde catches them on the stairs and says, 'Whatever you said, say it to me next time.'
plays.tells: A player asks about 'the Key' or 'the Seventh Bell' by name.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15 catches the half-second: she was afraid, not angry.
plays.later: S8: her last word mentions the Key outright; she has stopped pretending. S13: the Sexton will tell them what she was afraid of. Part 9, Situation 4: the Key stays in her palace vault until she leaves Hallowmere.
plays.keywords: key, tuning key, seventh bell, ysh, mention, reveal, accuse, maudrin, secret

plays.title: They read Maudrin with Insight, Detect Thoughts or Zone of Truth
plays.why: She is the antagonist, and casters reach for mind magic the moment she speaks.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums behind your teeth. Across the table Maudrin's eyes flick to you, then to your lips, and she smiles as though you had complimented her dress.
plays.response: Every spell in Corvane hums as it is cast, and Maudrin hears it. Detect Thoughts on her surface mind gives: 'Four of them. Ossa's. Not yet.' If the caster probes deeper she saves at +4; on a failure the caster sees a grey case on a chain, hears a lullaby, and feels her fear, and either way she knows, says “That was rude,” and ends the conversation. Zone of Truth fails near her chair: two silence-stones sit in the plinths of the dais, and the dimmed light shows the boundary before anyone casts. Insight DC 15 without magic tells them she means every promise and is leaving something out.
plays.consequence: They know she fears something she carries. She knows they read people.
plays.fallback: If no one has the spell, Insight alone gives the same last sentence.
plays.tells: A player asks “Is she lying?” or quietly names a spell.
plays.rules: Detect Thoughts (Maudrin's Wisdom save +4). Silence-stone field, 10 feet (Part 2.6 house rule). Insight DC 15. Counterspell if a spell would harm her.
plays.later: S22: the grey case and the lullaby make sense. S23: her first Counterspell goes to whoever cast Detect Thoughts on her tonight.
plays.keywords: detect thoughts, zone of truth, insight, read her, mind, lie, spell, probe, truth, silence-stone, dais

plays.title: They pay the Librarian for the diary's label
plays.why: The Librarian offers the answer outright for one true memory, and Edda's diary is the Act's prize.
plays.readAloud: The pages show your own face, then fill with handwriting that is almost yours: “You have asked a question with a memory behind it. Edda Thorne's diary is not on any shelf of this archive. Ask me the label, and I will tell you it, for one true memory.”
plays.response: The price is a memory the player is willing to give; the player names it and writes it in the ledger as a trade with the Librarian (not a Toll, not a Tithe, never redeemable). The answer is true: MIREL, LOST. Each further question costs another memory and gets a true but partial answer. If nobody will pay, the clue is not lost: Lysse cross-checks the Archive's accession lists and finds a Court receipt for 'one diary, relabelled'.
plays.consequence: They know what to look for in the vault: a cloth-wrapped book labelled MIREL, LOST.
plays.fallback: If the table stalls on the price, Lysse offers to pay it herself, and does; she has very little left to lose, and that should sting.
plays.tells: A player opens the wordless book, or asks Lysse where to look.
plays.rules: Study action, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 15 for Lysse's shortcut in an hour; on a failure she finds it by morning. Record Librarian trades as their own kind in the ledger.
plays.later: S5: they find the diary in a minute once inside. S22: if every other source is gone, the Librarian reads the Quiet Night page aloud for one true memory.
plays.keywords: librarian, sealed book, sealed stacks, question, label, diary, edda, mirel lost, memory, price, lysse

plays.title: They bargain for Mirel's Tongue
plays.why: The Librarian holds Mirel's Tongue and will trade it now, which saves the courier's bargain at Vael Tor.
plays.readAloud: A page turns by itself. “I keep the dream-bell's tongue because it belongs to whoever read it last. Give me a dream you have never told anyone, and you will be the last.”
plays.response: The price is a dream the giver has never told anyone; it is gone for good, and the player tells you (privately if they like) what it was. If they refuse the dream, the Librarian accepts a Gift instead (Part 2.7): something the giver values, given freely and never returned. The Tongue is a honey-coloured bronze clapper the length of a forearm, warm, and anyone who holds it yawns.
plays.consequence: The party carries Mirel's Tongue.
plays.fallback: If they refuse both prices, tell them plainly that the courier will repeat the offer at Vael Tor.
plays.tells: A player asks what else the Librarian keeps, or whether it would trade for a Tongue.
plays.rules: Record the dream as a Librarian trade, or the Gift as a Gift. Neither is Mirel's Toll: a Fear for one day is still owed when Mirel rings.
plays.later: S16B or S20: they can ring Mirel as soon as they reach the Sleeping Hall, and the Librarian's courier never comes. S9: a cart search at the north gate is now a real danger. S23: Maudrin wants every Tongue they carry.
plays.keywords: mirel, tongue, dream, librarian, trade, gift, bargain, dream bell, sleeping hall, buy

plays.title: They steal Mirel's Tongue from the Sealed Stacks
plays.why: A dream nobody has told is a steep price, and rogues like a reading stand with nothing guarding it.
plays.readAloud: The Tongue rests on a reading stand between two shelves, under a page that has written, very small: 'Do not.'
plays.response: Lifting it unseen is DC 16 Dexterity (Stealth) to reach the stand, or DC 16 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with Thieves' Tools to free it from the stand's clasp. Success: they have it, and the Librarian writes 'Then you are the last who read me' and closes; it answers no more questions this visit. Failure: the book slams, every warm spine in the Archive goes cold, and the Librarian fights only if someone keeps grabbing (The Librarian). The reading-room keepers fetch Hushmen in ten minutes, not three rounds.
