plays.consequence: On a success the party holds Mirel's Tongue and the Librarian is cold to them; on a failure the Tongue stays.
plays.fallback: If they fail and flee, Lysse covers for them with the keepers, and asks what on earth they were thinking.
plays.tells: A player asks where exactly the Tongue sits, or whether the book can see.
plays.rules: Stealth or Thieves' Tools DC 16. The Stacks are not silence-stone: spells work, but hum loudly in the quiet, and the Librarian hears them.
plays.later: S16B: if the theft failed, the courier still comes with the same offer. S22: even a cold Librarian keeps its word and reads the Quiet Night page for one true memory.
plays.keywords: steal, mirel, tongue, sealed stacks, sleight of hand, stealth, thieves tools, grab, librarian, snatch

plays.title: They bribe Ansel Quay for the vault door
plays.why: Ansel holds the key, wants to retire to the coast, and is obviously nervous: the easiest door in the book.
plays.readAloud: Ansel takes off the spectacles he doesn't need and polishes them. “I don't know what you mean,” he whispers. “And if I did, the service passage is unlocked between the second and third lamp-lightings. Hypothetically.”
plays.response: Ansel wants enough to retire to the coast, and the coast takes gold: 50 gp, or a Gift (something they value, freely given), or a believable promise of safety, meaning getting him and his cat out of the city when this is over. He opens the door, waits outside with his back turned, and gives them a quarter of an hour. For another 25 gp he sells the copy of the Tithe-Ledger he has been making for the Bellwrights; taking the copy sets off nothing. If anyone threatens him, he agrees to everything and tells Wren Caddock that night.
plays.consequence: The party is in the vault without a roll, and may hold Ansel's copy of the Ledger.
plays.fallback: If they can't afford him, he accepts a promise in writing, which he will hold them to.
plays.tells: Players ask who has the key, or Lysse mentions 'the steward who never needs his spectacles'.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Ansel starts Indifferent; a Gift or a safety promise makes him Friendly). Intimidation works and costs Wren's trust.
plays.later: S6: Ansel's copy contains the armory-payment entry that can win Rook's hearing, and Wren already knows who the party is when she approaches. Act IV (Part 9, Situation 4): Ansel knows Maudrin's routes from the palace to the Tor.
plays.keywords: ansel, quay, bribe, steward, archivist, key, vault, service passage, copy, ledger, gold, pay

plays.title: They break into the vault with tools or spells
plays.why: Lockpicks and Knock are the first tools most parties reach for.
plays.readAloud: The vault door is grey stone banded in iron. Ten feet out, the lamplight dims and there is a pressure in your ears like diving. Whatever hums behind your teeth goes quiet.
plays.response: The lock is DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with Thieves' Tools; a failure costs a minute. A Hushman passes every ten minutes (DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth) to wait in shadow). Fixed silence-stones in the frame and walls cover the door and the whole room: Knock fails, Invisibility and Pass without Trace are suppressed inside (they resume outside if concentration holds), and Dispel Magic cannot target a stone because a stone is not a spell. Prying a frame stone loose (AC 12, 10 HP) ends the field at the door, but stone cracking on stone sets off the alarm.
plays.consequence: They are in, and no Tonework works anywhere in the vault.
plays.fallback: If the lock beats them, Ansel comes out of the service passage with a lamp and a very guilty look.
plays.tells: A player asks about the lock, guards, or whether Knock or Invisibility will work.
plays.rules: Thieves' Tools DC 15. Stealth DC 13. Silence-stone house rule (Part 2.6): no spell can be cast in the field or produce an effect inside it. A fixed stone: AC 12, 10 HP.
plays.later: S7: Ilam Bray's service-passage key makes a second visit easy. Act IV (Situation 21): coming back for anything left on these shelves means this door again, with the Tithe Clock running.
plays.keywords: break in, lockpick, pick lock, thieves tools, knock, invisibility, pass without trace, dispel magic, silence-stone, vault door, sneak

plays.title: They open their own memory jar
plays.why: Every character has a jar with their name on it, and nobody can resist that.
plays.readAloud: The jar has your name on it in a clerk's tidy hand, and a date from when you were very small. It is warm. When you lift the stopper, the vault fills with a smell you had forgotten you knew.
plays.response: The memory returns whole. Describe it vividly from the character's earliest years, then ask the player to add one detail; it is theirs again. It carries a clue: the clerk who drew it wore a Hushman's grey glove, and the date is the year of a Tithe raid the character's family never mentioned (Part 7.7: it was not given willingly). Ansel's office tallies the jars each morning, so the empty one tells the Court who has been in.
plays.consequence: The memory is restored. The Court knows they opened it.
plays.fallback: If no player wants to, one jar hums louder until someone looks.
plays.tells: A player searches the shelves for their name.
plays.rules: Opening one's own jar restores the memory (Tithe, redeemable). Opening another person's jar only witnesses it and fades it; after three strangers it is spent. The S4 courtesy jar is on the newest shelf and opens the same way.
plays.later: S9: the Hallowmere Ledger asks what was in it. S24: Maudrin uses it: “I gave you that back, you know. I could have broken it.”
plays.keywords: jar, own jar, my name, memory, open, earliest memory, restore, tithe, courtesy jar

plays.title: They take Edda Thorne's diary
plays.why: Lysse asked for it, the Librarian pointed to it, and it is the true account of the Quiet Night.
plays.readAloud: “The seventh is not a bell. It is a lullaby with a voice, and the note beneath the note is the sound of something dreaming. Imber came to the Tower tonight with the Key, meaning to tune the seven into one long spring.”
plays.response: The diary is cloth-wrapped on the MIREL, LOST shelf: one minute to find if they know the label, ten minutes of searching if not, never missed. Read the full Quiet Night entry aloud (S5 box). Tell them plainly what else it holds, as the reveal-early rule requires: its later pages say six restored bells, each in its own voice, could hold the lullaby steady without waking anything. Taking it sets off no alarm; the Court knows it has gone by morning. If they would rather not risk it, they can read it and leave it: set the diary to 'Read and left behind', and the Court never learns.
plays.consequence: The party holds the true account of the Quiet Night and the first hint of the Concord.
plays.fallback: If they can't read bell-script or old Hesk, Lysse can; give her the moment.
plays.tells: A player asks for the shelf marked MIREL, LOST.
plays.rules: Search, Wisdom (Perception) DC 12 if they don't know the label; a failure only costs time.
plays.later: S13: the Sexton's confession matches it line for line, and he weeps to hear Edda's words. S22: it is a source for the truth of the Key. S24: Maudrin knows they have read what she read.
plays.keywords: diary, edda thorne, mirel lost, quiet night, read, take, steal, book, imber, lullaby, key

plays.title: They take Calla's Tongue from HARVEST, WITHHELD
plays.why: It is right there, warm, smelling of bread, and it is the only way to ring the Old Granary.
plays.readAloud: The moment the weight leaves the shelf, somewhere above you a bell-pull jerks, and a handbell with felt wrapped round its clapper starts thudding against its frame. Thud. Thud. Thud.
plays.response: The alarm is mechanical, not Tonework, so it works inside the silence-stone: the shelf is weighted, and any lift pulls the bell. A clever swap (an equal weight, DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand)) delays it by ten minutes instead of three rounds, but it still sounds. Hushmen arrive in three rounds (Vault Alarm), so the party should be moving by round two. For the next two days, four Hushmen search every cart leaving the city.
plays.consequence: The party carries Calla's Tongue and the Court is hunting it.
plays.fallback: If they freeze when the alarm sounds, Ansel's voice from the service passage hisses, “This way. Now.”
plays.tells: A player unwraps the cloth on the HARVEST, WITHHELD shelf.
plays.rules: Alarm: Hushmen in 3 rounds. Sleight of Hand DC 15 for a weight-swap (delay, not prevention). Searching the shelf first shows the bell-pull without a roll.
plays.later: S9: Calla can be rung at Kell's Crossing, three days north; Bet Ostrow is the natural Gift. S9: cart searches at the gate for two days. S15: Isolde asks for Calla's Tongue too. S23: Maudrin wants every Tongue they carry.
plays.keywords: calla, tongue, harvest withheld, take, steal, alarm, shelf, bread, granary, kell's crossing

plays.title: They take the Tithe-Ledger or Ansel's copy
plays.why: Rook wants it, and the master book of who gave what is the strongest evidence in the city.
plays.readAloud: The Ledger is as thick as a doorstep, chained to its stand with a plain iron chain. The newest pages are still damp at the edges.
plays.response: Lifting the original pulls the same alarm as Calla's Tongue. Ansel's copy (sold for 25 gp) sets off nothing and is just as good as evidence. Finding one entry takes ten minutes without a roll. Worth finding: Ser Haldric's armory payments ('for H., at the Chancellor's pleasure: three heartkeeps, quarterly'); Mara Bray, Tithed of 'her son', 408 SS; Lysse Carrow, twice, under other people's names; each party member's jars.
plays.consequence: The party holds the evidence that can break Haldric, and a map of whose memories are where.
plays.fallback: If they skip it, Ansel's copy can still reach Rook through Wren before the hearing, for a price.
plays.tells: A player goes to the reading stand, or asks Ansel about copies.
plays.rules: Study, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 15 finds an entry in a minute; otherwise ten minutes, no roll. Taking the original: alarm, Hushmen in 3 rounds, cart searches for two days.
plays.later: S6: the armory-payment entry wins Rook's hearing. S7: Mara Bray's entry says Jonah's mother is alive and a Blank. S9: with Ilam's roster as well, they can name every Hushman at the north gate.
plays.keywords: ledger, tithe-ledger, book, copy, evidence, haldric, payment, entry, records, names, steal, ansel

plays.title: They find the EXPORT — VENNMARK column
plays.why: Anyone reading the Ledger closely, or a Stormborn who reads Common, will notice a column in the wrong language.
plays.readAloud: The last column on each page is narrower than the rest and ruled in newer ink. Its heading is in Common, not Hesk: EXPORT — VENNMARK. Beside some names, a tick and a ship: Gilded Heron. Saltglass. Gilded Heron again.
plays.response: The Court sells 'surplus' Tithed memories to Master Orsolo Venn's coster, and they are shipped through the Seam to Athkatla: heartkeeps, mostly, the red-wax weights. Blanks' memories may be sitting in an Amnian noble's cabinet right now. Reckoner Sela Maunt in Pellmoor could confirm the weights from the stamps, and Venn's own counting-house ledgers would prove the trade.
plays.consequence: The memory trade is not only the Court's crime. The party has a reason to go back to Pellmoor.
plays.fallback: If nobody notices, Lysse does, and asks what 'Vennmark' means.
plays.tells: A player asks where the Tithed memories go, or reads the Ledger page by page.
plays.rules: Study, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 12 to notice it if nobody asks about exports; a character who reads Common notices it without a roll.
plays.later: S7: telling the Blanks is a spark. S9: a detour to Pellmoor can confront Venn (Venn hostile, Landing clock moves). S22: exposing the trade to the Harpers or the Dawn Mission earns the Stormborn ally. Act V: in the Empty Choir, the export trade grows.
plays.keywords: export, vennmark, venn, coster, athkatla, amn, ship, gilded heron, column, trade, smuggle, heartkeeps, faerun

plays.title: They take other people's memory jars
plays.why: Players who care about Bet, Lysse or the Blanks will want their memories back.
plays.readAloud: The shelves go on further than the lamp reaches. OSTROW, B. 340 SS. BRAY, M. 408 SS. Each jar hums a different note, like a choir that has lost its place.
plays.response: Jars are not weighted like the Calla shelf; a few can leave in a satchel without the alarm, and Ansel's morning tally finds the gaps. Only the owner can restore a memory: Bet must open her own jar to remember ringing Calla at nine, and Mara Bray hers to know her son. Anyone else who opens a jar only witnesses it and fades it, and a dropped jar scatters the memory for good. Lysse's two jars are filed under other names (MORROW, T. and HADE, E.); Study DC 15 matches her hand in the 'reason given' column.
plays.consequence: The party carries other people's memories, and the responsibility that comes with them.
plays.fallback: If they hesitate over whose jars to take, Lysse asks quietly whether hers are here.
plays.tells: A player searches for a friend's name rather than their own.
plays.rules: Witnessing another's jar fades it (three times and it is spent). Destroying a jar scatters the memory; it does not restore it. Study DC 15 for Lysse's jars.
plays.later: S6: Bet, given her jar, remembers the Last Ringing and asks to ring Calla again (S9). S7: Mara opening her jar lets her know Jonah. S30: Lysse recovers her memories and writes the true history.
plays.keywords: jars, other people, bet, ostrow, mara bray, lysse, steal jars, free memories, blanks, return

plays.title: They set off the alarm without taking anything
plays.why: A careless lift, a cracked stone or a dropped jar is easy in a dim room.
plays.readAloud: Thud. Thud. Thud. Above you, boots on stone, and someone shouting for lamps.
plays.response: Hushmen arrive in three rounds (Vault Alarm). They want arrests and an intact vault; they block the doors rather than fight among the jars. The party can surrender, fight out through the service passage, or bluff that Ansel let them in (DC 15 Charisma (Deception); Ansel will not thank them). Nothing is missing, so nobody searches carts afterward, but the Court knows faces were in its vault.
plays.consequence: The Court tightens its watch on the vault; the party may be identified.
plays.fallback: If capture looks certain, Ansel throws the service-passage bolt from the far side and pretends he never did.
plays.tells: A failed check near the Calla shelf, the reading stand, or a frame stone.
plays.rules: Hushmen in 3 rounds. Deception DC 15. Grappled. Tonework fails inside the vault, so casters must fight their way to the door first.
plays.later: S6: Haldric uses the break-in to argue on the Dawn Steps that Rook's 'evidence' is stolen. S7: Ilam's key still opens the service passage if they need another try.
plays.keywords: alarm, caught, hushmen, fight, escape, surrender, bluff, vault, service passage, trapped

plays.title: They take Captain Rook's commission
plays.why: Rook is honest, desperate and offers protection; she is the first authority in Hallowmere who asks rather than takes.
plays.readAloud: “I don't have time for pleasantries. The Court is rotten, and I'm not allowed to say so, because the men who could say it have been Tithed. So I'm asking you. Will you help me find out what's in the Tithe-Ledger? Not for the Court. For the people who've forgotten their own children.”
plays.response: Rook wants a copy of the Ledger or the original before the oath-hearing in two days. In return she gives one day of protection (a Dawn Order writ that Hushmen must honour until dusk) and an escort of two knights. She is honest and she is using them, and says so if asked. If they already hold the Ledger or Ansel's copy (S5), she reads the payment entries in silence and then says, “We.”
plays.consequence: The party works for the Dawn Order's captain. Haldric knows by evening.
plays.fallback: If they won't commit, Rook says the hearing goes ahead regardless and they can watch her lose.
plays.tells: Players ask what she needs, what she offers, or whether she can be trusted.
plays.rules: Rook starts Friendly to anyone who protects the innocent. Influence DC 15 to keep the escort a second day.
plays.later: S6: the hearing turns on what they bring. S9: if Rook wins, she lends Vaer's Tongue and the chain-key. S22: Rook and her knights are an ally only if she won.
plays.keywords: rook, dessa, captain, dawn order, commission, job, ledger, protection, escort, hire

plays.title: They present Haldric's payments at the oath-duel
plays.why: The party holds the Ledger, Ansel's copy or a witness, and the Dawn Steps are where it counts.
plays.readAloud: The Dawn Steps are crowded to the lamps. Rook and Haldric stand three steps apart in the grey light, swords laid sheathed at their feet. A herald calls for the first question from the crowd.
plays.response: Each knight swears 'I have not sold this Order's protection to the Court' and answers three questions chosen by the players. Rook admits small compromises and denies selling protection. Haldric denies payment smoothly until he is confronted with the armory-payment entry, Ansel's copy, or a corroborated witness (Eld's note plus the party's testimony counts as one). Shown the entry, he looks once toward the palace, then refuses to answer, and refusing loses: he is stripped of his sword and his knights step away from him. If Ossa's Tongue was in the armory, Rook hands it straight back to the party.
plays.consequence: Rook wins. Haldric is disgraced; Rook holds the armory and Vaer's Tongue (set Ossa's Tongue to 'With the party' if it was there).
plays.fallback: If the players fumble the questions, Rook asks the last one herself: 'Ser Haldric, what does the line for H. in this book mean?'
plays.tells: A player asks how the duel works, or rehearses their three questions.
plays.rules: Finding the entry: ten minutes, no roll; Study, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 15 to have it ready before the hearing starts. A failure means a recess or another witness, never lost evidence.
plays.later: S9: Rook opens Vaer's Belfry and gives them the chain-key, and the Dawn Order will not enforce a Silence Warrant. S22: Rook and her knights hold the ridge. S23: Haldric and both Dawn Order knights are absent from the Strike, leaving Maudrin and four Hushmen (a much smaller fight than the full Strike).
plays.keywords: oath-duel, duel, hearing, evidence, ledger, haldric, rook, dawn steps, questions, prove, payment, win

plays.title: The hearing goes ahead without proof
plays.why: The vault went badly or the party never went in, and Rook will not postpone.
plays.readAloud: Haldric answers every question beautifully, with a little bow to the crowd after each one. When it is over, he offers Rook his hand. She doesn't take it.
plays.response: Rook's accusation fails for now; Haldric keeps his office and is gracious about it, which is worse. Tell the players this door stays open: Dawn Order law allows a second hearing with new evidence within a month. Haldric now knows exactly who stood with Rook.
plays.consequence: Rook's case fails for now. Haldric holds the armory.
plays.fallback: Rook buys them a drink afterward and says, 'Get me the book. I'll call it again.'
plays.tells: The party arrives at the Steps empty-handed, or with only suspicion.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15 on Haldric: relief, not confidence.
plays.later: S9: Rook can still be talked into a quiet loan of Vaer's Tongue (Influence DC 15), but the armory is Haldric's. If they bring the Ledger later in Act II, rerun the hearing and set the duel to 'Rook won'. S23: if it is never reopened, Haldric and his knights ride with Maudrin.
plays.keywords: no evidence, lose, fail, hearing, duel, haldric wins, rook loses, reopen, recess

plays.title: They support Ser Haldric
plays.why: Haldric is charming and offers alliance; a table that distrusts Rook, or wants Court favour, may take it.
plays.readAloud: Haldric catches you on the stair afterward, polishing a gauntlet that is already clean. “For the good of all, I'd be grateful for friends who see clearly. The dawn will come. It only needs the right hands.”
plays.response: With the party behind him, Haldric wins, and the Dawn Order accepts the Court's control of the city. Then he asks for one thing: Bellwright names. Only names the party actually gives are endangered; each one is a Hushman raid within three days. He keeps his promises exactly as long as no better offer arrives.
plays.consequence: Haldric wins the duel. Rook is humiliated. The Bellwrights learn who helped.
plays.fallback: If they waver, Haldric offers them the armory's 'safekeeping' of any Tongue they carry, which is the Court's armory in all but name.
plays.tells: Players warm to Haldric's courtesy, or ask what he can offer them.
plays.rules: Haldric starts Friendly to allies. Record in the Bargain Log what he promised and what they gave.
plays.later: S9: the Dawn Order enforces any Silence Warrant and Vaer's Belfry is shut to them. S18A: Corin Aldeth knows who gave names and is cold. S23: Haldric and two knights ride in the Strike at full strength; even so, if the party holds the Key there, Haldric hesitates, and that still breaks the line.
plays.keywords: support haldric, side with haldric, betray rook, alliance, bellwright names, informer, court favour

plays.title: They stay out of the duel
plays.why: It looks like Dawn Order business, and the party has its own goals.
plays.readAloud: By the evening lamps the news is everywhere: the Captain's accusation failed. By morning there are Hushmen at every door of the Archive.
plays.response: Rook's unsupported accusation fails. Court patrols tighten: Hushmen at the Archive doors and a checkpoint on the Hall of Tithes steps. Rook does not blame them aloud. She remembers.
plays.consequence: Rook's case fails for now and the city gets tighter.
plays.fallback: If the players want back in, Rook will reopen it the day they bring her the book.
plays.tells: “That's their fight.” Or the party is busy elsewhere on the day.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 (up from 13) to move unseen in the upper city for the rest of the Act.
plays.later: S7: the Hushmen line forms faster. S9: Rook might still help if asked (Influence DC 15), but she has nothing to give. S23: Haldric and his knights ride with Maudrin unless the case is reopened.
plays.keywords: stay out, ignore, not our business, skip duel, neutral, avoid

plays.title: They use Zone of Truth or Detect Thoughts on the knights
plays.why: Clerics and bards at level 3–4 have exactly the spells a lie-hearing seems to call for.
plays.readAloud: Two heralds in faded dawn-yellow stand at the top of the Steps holding grey stone rods. Around each knight the lamplight is a shade dimmer than it ought to be.
plays.response: An oath-court allows no Tonework: by Dawn Order law each knight stands in a herald's silence-stone field (10 feet), so Zone of Truth and Detect Thoughts on the knights fail, visibly, and casting at them is contempt (the caster's side loses one question). Off the Steps, magic works. Detect Thoughts on Haldric is negated by his silence-stone shield the first time each day; a second casting shows him thinking 'She won't let them break me. She promised.' Zone of Truth on a willing witness (Eld, Ansel or Wren) before the hearing counts: the herald accepts a witness who stood in a Zone as corroboration.
plays.consequence: Magic can find and support evidence. It never replaces it.
plays.fallback: If the caster feels cheated, let the herald say aloud why the rods exist: 'A knight's word is weighed by men, not tones.'
plays.tells: A player asks whether Zone of Truth is allowed, or casts it from the crowd.
plays.rules: Silence-stone field, 10 feet (house rule). Haldric's shield negates the first spell that targets only him each day; area spells are unaffected. Zone of Truth: Charisma save.
plays.later: S23: Haldric remembers who tried to read him, and keeps his shield raised toward that caster.
plays.keywords: zone of truth, detect thoughts, spell, magic, lie, truth, oath, herald, rods, silence-stone, shield, read mind

plays.title: They attack Haldric on the Dawn Steps
plays.why: Haldric is smug, the party may know he's guilty, and the evidence isn't landing.
plays.readAloud: The herald drops his rod with a crack like a bell that cannot ring. “Order! Order on the Steps!” Haldric's knights close around him in a wall of grey steel.
plays.response: Violence at an oath-court voids the hearing: the herald calls it, Haldric's knights close ranks, and Rook roars at the party to stand down. If they keep going, use Dawn Steps Brawl. Haldric fights to disarm and arrest, then plays the wronged man perfectly to the crowd. If Haldric dies, set him Dead and say so plainly.
plays.consequence: The hearing is void. The party is a named enemy, and Rook is furious.
plays.fallback: If it turns deadly, Rook steps in front of the party with her sword sheathed and her arms wide, and nobody on the Steps will strike her.
plays.tells: Weapons drawn in the crowd, or a spell readied at the herald.
plays.rules: Knights: Parry reaction. Haldric's shield negates the first spell that targets only him each day. Grappled, Prone.
plays.later: S9: Rook lends them nothing until they make amends (a public apology on the Steps, Influence DC 15). S23: Haldric and his knights ride with Maudrin; if Haldric died here, the Strike has two knights and no Haldric, and no hesitation breaks the line.
plays.keywords: attack haldric, fight, kill haldric, brawl, violence, dawn steps, knights, duel fight

plays.title: They hear Wren's confession
plays.why: Wren chooses them in Bet's bakery; what they do with a spy who gave up Tam Harrow is a real choice.
plays.readAloud: “I'm sorry. I have to tell you something you won't like. I've been giving the Court names. Bellwright names, and one from Pellmoor: a ferryman called Tam Harrow. Two years now. I'd stop if I could, but they've got my daughter.”
plays.response: Wren has also warned the Bellwrights of several raids, which is why some survived. She asks nothing for herself, only that Tessa be taken out of the city. If they listen or forgive, she gives the dormitory room, the evening shift change (third lamp-lighting), and Ilam Bray as the Hushman who knows the service entrance. If they hand her to the Hushmen, set Wren to 'Exposed to the Court': Tessa is moved to a Tithe-house and Wren is Tithed within a week.
plays.consequence: The party knows who gave up Tam Harrow, and has a way to Tessa.
plays.fallback: If the party is cold, Wren leaves the dormitory plan on the counter wrapped in a loaf and walks out.
plays.tells: A freckled woman with sewing in her lap asks to sit down, then can't start.
plays.rules: Insight DC 12: she is telling the truth and terrified. No Influence is needed; she is Friendly to anyone who isn't cruel, and breaks if someone is.
plays.later: S7: Ilam Bray's name ties Wren's plan to Jonah. S28: whether to tell Ila is the party's call; Ila trusts people who tell her hard truths. Act IV: Ansel is loyal to Wren, not Maudrin, and knows Maudrin's routes. S29: Wren is forgiven, or is not.
plays.keywords: wren, caddock, confession, spy, informer, tam harrow, betrayal, forgive, daughter, tessa, bakery

plays.title: They get Tessa out of the Hall of Tithes
plays.why: A rescue with a known room and shift change is the kind of plan players love.
plays.readAloud: The clerks' dormitory smells of ink and boiled cabbage. Two grey-gloved men lean on either side of a door at the end of the corridor, bored, counting the minutes to the shift bell.
plays.response: Three good routes: a forged transfer order (DC 14 Charisma (Deception) on the guards, or DC 14 Intelligence check with a Forgery Kit to make one that needs no talking); a negotiated exchange through Ansel, who 'misfiles' Tessa as a kitchen girl for 25 gp; or a kitchen evacuation (a grease fire, smoke, a well-placed Prestidigitation). Failure alerts the guards and starts a chase through the lanes, never an automatic Tithe (Tessa's Guards). Bet Ostrow hides Tessa overnight above the bakery and Wren has a cart out at dawn. If Ila was arrested after S3, she is in the next room, and the same plan frees her too.
plays.consequence: Tessa is out. Wren is free of the Court's hold and becomes the party's ally.
plays.fallback: If the plan collapses, Ilam Bray, on the corridor shift, looks at Tessa, looks at the party, and opens the service door.
plays.tells: The party asks Wren for the layout, or starts forging papers.
plays.rules: Deception DC 14, or Forgery Kit DC 14. Stealth DC 13 in the corridor; Pass without Trace works (no silence-stones here). One night in the city: Tithe Clock +1. If your table has no child peril, Tessa is Wren's adult sister.
plays.later: S9: Wren's Bellwright route can carry a Tongue past the cart searches. S18A: Corin trusts the party because the Bellwrights trust Wren. S29: 'Wren gets her daughter out.'
plays.keywords: tessa, rescue, hall of tithes, dormitory, forge, forgery, transfer order, kitchen, fire, distraction, child, wren

plays.title: They are kind to Bet Ostrow
plays.why: Bet feeds anyone who looks hungry, and players adopt her on sight.
plays.readAloud: Bet presses a heel of warm bread into your hands before you've asked. A child at the counter jingles something in a pocket, a little brass bell, and Bet goes perfectly still with the knife in the loaf.
plays.response: Bet chatters, then stops mid-sentence and cries without knowing why; she freezes at any small bell. Her hands still know the harvest-bell's tune: if anyone hums a few notes of a harvest-song, her fingers tap the rhythm on the counter. If the party brought her jar from the vault (S5) and she opens it herself, she remembers ringing Calla at nine and asks, very quietly, whether she could do it again.
plays.consequence: Bet trusts them, and her bakery becomes a safe house.
plays.fallback: If nobody engages, Bet sends a loaf to their lodgings with a note: 'You looked hungry.'
plays.tells: A player accepts the bread, asks her name, or asks why she is crying.
plays.rules: Heroic Inspiration: giving Bet back her own memory freely earns it (v6 generosity rule).
plays.later: S9: Bet is the natural Gift-recipient when Calla rings, or the Ringer herself if she remembers. Act IV (Situation 21): Bet knows which carts leave the city unsearched. S30: Bet cries when she hears a bell, and this time she knows why.
plays.keywords: bet, ostrow, baker, bakery, bread, kind, bell, cry, calla, harvest, jar

plays.title: They calm the crowd before the line moves
plays.why: Hundreds of grieving people and a line of Hushmen: most parties try words first.
plays.readAloud: The Hall of Tithes is surrounded. Hundreds of people, grey-faced, holding up old drawings and wooden toys, shouting names they cannot quite remember. They do not riot. They only stand and ask, over and over, “Who was she? Who was I?” The Hushmen are forming a line.
plays.response: The Blanks follow anyone who promises to help them recover their memories, and they hold that person to it. Calming them is Influence (Persuasion) DC 16 by one speaker, with Help from others; a promise backed by something real (jars from the vault, the Ledger's names) gives advantage. Success: the crowd sits down on the steps in silence, which the Hushmen have no procedure for, and Sergeant Orla Gaunt orders the line to hold. Failure: the crowd surges, the Hushmen arrest anyone who interferes, and the party must pick a side now.
plays.consequence: The Blanks trust the party, and expect them to keep their promise.
plays.fallback: If the speech stalls, a Blank at the front asks the speaker their name, forgets it, and asks again; the crowd laughs, and the tension breaks a little.
plays.tells: A player climbs onto something to be seen, or asks who leads the crowd.
plays.rules: Influence DC 16 for the crowd; Help gives advantage. Calm Emotions or Thaumaturgy can also give advantage (see the spells play).
plays.later: S22: the Blanks march. S23: they break the Hushmen's line by numbers. S28–30: every promise made on these steps is asked about by name.
plays.keywords: crowd, blanks, calm, speech, persuade, promise, help, protest, hall of tithes, steps

plays.title: They fight the Hushmen line
plays.why: The line moves on unarmed grieving people; many tables will not stand by.
plays.readAloud: Six grey gloves come up together. Where they strike, there is no sound at all, and that is the worst part.
plays.response: The Hushmen want arrests, not deaths, and so do the Blanks: area damage near the crowd hits Blanks too (Commoners, 4 HP each). Use the Hushmen Line. Give the party a way to end it fast: Sergeant Gaunt withdraws when half her line is down or the party holds the Hall's doors. Afterward the steps belong to the Blanks, and to the party.
plays.consequence: The party is the Blanks' champion and the Court's named enemy.
plays.fallback: If it turns bloody, Captain Rook's knights arrive on the far side of the square and the Sergeant decides she has been outnumbered.
plays.tells: Weapons out, or a player steps between a Hushman and a Blank.
plays.rules: Hushmen: Pack Tactics, grapple. Silence-stone gloves silence only their own strikes. Blanks are Commoners (4 HP).
plays.later: S9: the north gate is reinforced (Gate Sweep at every gate). S22: the Blanks march. S23: they break the line by numbers.
plays.keywords: fight, attack hushmen, line, protect, combat, battle, defend blanks, sergeant

plays.title: They reunite Jonah and Ilam Bray
plays.why: A boy with a wooden bird and a Hushman who stops when he sees it: the scene asks to be finished.
plays.readAloud: “That's my carving. I made it for my son. I don't know his name anymore. I've tried. I don't know why I can't remember. Is he in there? In the crowd? Please. I need to see him.”
plays.response: Bring Jonah to the edge of the line, or Ilam to the boy. Neither remembers the other's name. The bird does it: Ilam turns it over, finds the notch where his knife slipped, and Jonah says, very literally, “You made that.” Ilam takes off his silence-stone gloves on the spot and drops them on the stones. He gives the party a key to the Tithe-Ledger Room's service passage and the Hushman roster: every name, post and shift.
plays.consequence: Ilam deserts the Hushmen. The party holds a vault key and the roster.
plays.fallback: If the party misses the moment, Jonah walks to Ilam by himself and holds up the bird.
plays.tells: A player notices Ilam staring at the bird, or asks Jonah where he got it.
plays.rules: No check if Jonah trusts the party (he attaches to whoever is kind). Stealth DC 13 to get Ilam out of the line before his Sergeant notices.
plays.later: S9: the roster says which gate and shift to avoid. S22: Ilam holds the Tor's southern road. S23: Ilam stands between Jonah and the fight, and Jonah sees his father clearly. S30: Jonah remembers his mother's face, if she is found.
plays.keywords: jonah, ilam, bray, reunite, father, son, wooden bird, carving, family, hushman, desert

plays.title: They attack Ilam Bray
plays.why: A gloved Hushman walking toward a child looks like a threat to a table that has learned to hate Hushmen.
plays.readAloud: The crowd's murmur stops dead. Jonah screams a word you don't know, and somewhere in the crowd a woman's voice says it too.
plays.response: The crowd turns on the party: they are now the villains of the Blanks. Ilam does not fight back beyond covering his face; if he is killed, set him Dead and say so plainly. Jonah runs into the crowd and is taken into Court custody by nightfall unless someone else reaches him first.
plays.consequence: The Blanks turn against the party.
plays.fallback: If the player hesitates mid-swing, let Ilam drop his gloves first; nobody attacks a man with bare hands raised.
plays.tells: A player readies an attack as Ilam steps out of the line.
plays.rules: Ilam: Hushman (Tough). The crowd will not fight, but it blocks, shouts, and remembers faces.
plays.later: S22: the Blanks will not march, and some inform on the party. S23: if Jonah is in custody, Maudrin brings him to the ridge as a hostage, and freeing him costs one Tongue or the Strike.
plays.keywords: attack ilam, kill hushman, strike, mistake, wrong person, fight, ilam bray

plays.title: They leave Jonah in the crowd
plays.why: The party has bigger aims, or simply doesn't notice one boy among hundreds.
plays.readAloud: Later, you remember the bird: a small wooden shape held up above the heads, going away from you toward the carts.
plays.response: The sweep takes Jonah into Court custody as a Blank. He goes quietly, holding the bird. Ilam watches the cart go and says nothing; his Sergeant tells him to hold the line, and he does.
plays.consequence: Jonah is in Court custody. Ilam stays a Hushman.
plays.fallback: If a player asks later, Ilam can be found drinking alone at the Shuttered Lamp, asking strangers whether they've seen a boy with a bird.
plays.tells: The party heads for the vault, the Archive or the gate while the sweep begins.
plays.later: S9: Jonah is in the Hall of Tithes until then; a rescue like Tessa's still works (same guards, same shift change). S23: Maudrin brings him to the ridge as a hostage; freeing him costs one Tongue or the Strike.
plays.keywords: leave, ignore, abandon, jonah, custody, sweep, cart, walk away

plays.title: They take Jonah somewhere safe without his father
plays.why: Saving the child is obvious; trusting the Hushman isn't.
plays.readAloud: Jonah holds your hand and the bird in the other, very tightly. “Is the man with the gloves coming?” he asks. Then, a street later: “Is he coming?”
plays.response: Jonah goes with whoever is kind. Bet Ostrow's attic, the Dawn Mission's lodging (if Aurelie is in the city) or Rook's barracks will take him. He asks every hour whether the man with the gloves is coming. Ilam keeps looking, and a reunion can still happen before they leave the city.
plays.consequence: Jonah is safe. Ilam is still a Hushman, searching.
plays.fallback: If nobody knows where to take him, Bet does: 'Attic's warm. He can have the cat.'
plays.tells: A player picks Jonah up and heads away from the line.
plays.rules: One night in the city: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S9: Ilam finds the bakery; play the reunion there and set Jonah to 'Reunited' and Ilam to 'Deserted, an ally'. S23: a safe Jonah is no hostage. S30: his mother still needs finding.
plays.keywords: hide jonah, protect, safe house, bakery, take him, child, shelter, bet

plays.title: They look for Jonah's mother
plays.why: The Ledger or Ilam's roster names Mara Bray, and players want the family whole.
plays.readAloud: Mara Bray sits on the steps with an empty frame in her lap. She is very polite. She asks your names, forgets them, and asks again.
plays.response: The Ledger (S5) or Ilam names her: Mara Bray, Tithed of 'her son' in 408 SS, in this crowd. She does not know Jonah and he does not know her; the meeting is gentle and painful, and nothing more. Her memory is a red-wax heartkeep jar in the vault, unless the EXPORT — VENNMARK column has a tick by her name, in which case it sailed on the Gilded Heron last season. Only Mara opening her own jar brings Jonah back to her.
plays.consequence: The family is three people on paper, and one jar away from three people in fact.
plays.fallback: If they don't look, Ilam asks them to, the night before they leave.
plays.tells: A player asks “Where's his mother?”
plays.rules: Lesser Restoration and Remove Curse do nothing for a Blank: a Tithed memory is not a condition or a curse. Only the owner opening the jar restores it.
plays.later: S9: a second vault visit with Ilam's key can bring her jar out. Act V or beyond: if her jar was exported, it is in Athkatla, through the Seam. S30: Jonah remembers his mother's face, if she is found.
plays.keywords: mara, bray, mother, jonah's mother, blank, jar, family, find, ledger, heartkeep

plays.title: They use magic on the crowd or the line
plays.why: Calm Emotions, Suggestion and Silence are all on level 3–4 lists and all look made for this square.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums across the square, and every grey glove in the line turns toward the sound.
plays.response: Calm Emotions on the crowd's front ranks gives advantage on the DC 16 Influence and ends Frightened in the area. Suggestion on Sergeant Gaunt ('send your men home; there's nothing to arrest here') works if she fails her Wisdom save; she obeys and is furious afterward. The Silence spell over the line is sacramental here: the Hushmen hesitate for one round, because nobody has ever turned the Court's holy quiet against them. Thaumaturgy lets one speaker be heard across the whole square.
plays.consequence: Magic can win the crowd a night. The caster is marked.
plays.fallback: If a spell fails, the hum alone makes the front rank of Blanks turn and look at the caster with hope, which is pressure enough.
plays.tells: A caster asks how many people a spell can cover, or whether the Sergeant can be charmed.
plays.rules: Calm Emotions (Charisma save, unwilling only). Suggestion (Gaunt's Wisdom save +2). Silence the spell is not silence-stone: Tonework works outside its sphere. Lesser Restoration does not restore Tithed memories. Every spell hums, so the line knows who cast.
plays.later: S9: the caster's description is at every gate, with +2 to the DC of any bluff there.
plays.keywords: calm emotions, suggestion, silence, thaumaturgy, spell, magic, crowd, charm, sergeant, hushmen

plays.title: They tell the Blanks their memories are shipped abroad
plays.why: A party that found the EXPORT — VENNMARK column (S5) has a truth that answers 'Who was I?' in the worst way.
plays.readAloud: It goes through the crowd like a dropped lamp through dry reeds. “Sold?” “Across the sea?” Somebody starts to scream a name, and doesn't stop.
plays.response: Half the crowd surges for the Hall's doors and the line moves at once (Hushmen Line, with Blanks in the way). The other half turns to any Stormborn in the party: “Your people have them?” A Faerûnian character is mobbed, not hurt, and must answer. The Court hears what was said within the hour.
plays.consequence: The Blanks know about the export trade, and the Court knows the party knows.
plays.fallback: If the surge gets dangerous, Ilam Bray drops his gloves and starts helping people off the steps, and others follow.
plays.tells: A player mentions Venn, Athkatla, or 'the ships' in front of the crowd.
plays.rules: Influence DC 18 to calm them after this (raised from 16).
plays.later: S9: a detour to Pellmoor to confront Venn becomes a promise to keep. S22: the Blanks march, but some want to march on Pellmoor's quays instead.
plays.keywords: export, vennmark, venn, ships, athkatla, sold, tell crowd, reveal, riot, faerun, stormborn

plays.title: They trace the courier
plays.why: A shaking one-line letter from 'I.V.' begs the question who carried it.
plays.readAloud: The courier is a trapper in reindeer hide with frost-burn on both cheeks, and he will not sit near the fire. “Not mine to explain,” he says. “I was paid to carry it. The sister wrote it. The voice said it.”
plays.response: He is Edrin Moss, a Glassreach trapper. A DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check, or a drink and Influence DC 15, gets the rest: he was paid by Wyn Talla, an old woman at the forest's edge whose sister Maren has been Stilled in the glass for 380 years. A voice in the glass told Wyn what to write, called itself 'I.V.', and promised Maren would move again. On a failure Edrin leaves at dawn and they can follow his tracks north. That afternoon two Hushmen and a Court agent try to take Edrin off the street (Courier Snatch): Isolde wants to read the letter too.
plays.consequence: They know where to start in Glassreach (Wyn Talla's hut, beside Yara's camp) and that the Court is interested.
plays.fallback: If they don't ask, Edrin asks them, on his way out, whether they know what year it is up north. He's never sure.
plays.tells: A player asks where the courier went, or who paid him.
plays.rules: Investigation DC 15, or Influence DC 15 (Edrin is Indifferent; Friendly if paid or warmed).
plays.later: S10: Wyn waits at Yara's camp and asks them to free Maren. S11: Maren is one of the Stilled adults; waking her gently is the kind route. S15: if Maren wakes, Wyn is first to bring the Stilled bread.
plays.keywords: courier, letter, trace, investigate, trapper, edrin, who sent it, i.v., glassreach, wyn talla

plays.title: They question Isolde about Maudrin's last word
plays.why: Isolde delivers Maudrin's message in person, and it raises more questions than it answers.
plays.readAloud: “Thank you for your curiosity. It is, after all, why I invited you. When you come back from the north, I will be waiting, and so will the Key. Give my regards to the Glass Sexton. He was once family, and he will not thank you for disturbing him.”
plays.response: Isolde reads it word for word and watches what it does to their faces. Asked what it means, she gives the truth as she knows it: the Glass Sexton is Imber Vesk, High Sexton on the Quiet Night, and 'once family' means exactly that. She does not know what the Key is, and that bothers her. She mentions, idly, that the North Road is cold and that she has never liked the cold.
plays.consequence: They know the Sexton is a Vesk, and that someone will follow them north.
plays.fallback: If they ignore her, she leaves the message pinned to their door with a silver hairpin, which is worth 5 gp and is clearly a test.
plays.tells: Players ask what 'he was once family' means, or what the Key is.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15: she is going north herself, and isn't pleased about it. Influence DC 15 (Isolde's Intelligence 12) to learn when: within a day of their leaving.
plays.later: S9: Isolde follows with a Hushman escort. S13: the Sexton asks who rules the Court, and the answer is his own blood. S15: Isolde arrives at the thaw.
plays.keywords: isolde, drave, maudrin, message, last word, key, glass sexton, family, vesk, question

plays.title: They turn Isolde into an informant
plays.why: Players who learned about her son, or her quiet sales to the Ironhorn, have leverage on the Court's best gossip.
plays.readAloud: Isolde sets her glass down for the first time all evening. “Careful. People who say that to me usually want something. What do you want, and what will you give my son?”
plays.response: Two levers work: her son's safety (a place outside the city, such as Pellmoor under Brannagh Wick's pilots, or Rook's protection) and her secret (she sells Tithed memories to the Ironhorn Compact; Ansel's copy of the Ledger shows the gaps if they look). Either moves her to Friendly; then Influence DC 15 seals it. She will still be sent north, because refusing would expose her, but she brings only two Hushmen and warns the party what the Court wants.
plays.consequence: Isolde is their informant inside the Court, for as long as it protects her son.
plays.fallback: If they push too hard, she laughs, agrees to nothing, and remembers they tried.
plays.tells: A player brings up her son, or what she sells and to whom.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15, only after a real offer or real leverage. Record in the Bargain Log: Isolde's son's safety.
plays.later: S9: she follows anyway, leaving a note at the first waystation naming her escort. S15: she asks for the Frost Tongue in front of her Hushmen, then offers a private way to 'lose' it. S21: she warns them a day before Maudrin leaves Hallowmere.
plays.keywords: isolde, informant, turn, blackmail, leverage, son, ironhorn, deal, spy, double agent

plays.title: They ignore the letter
plays.why: Some tables refuse the hook, or want Brassfall, Vael Tor or Pellmoor first.
plays.readAloud: A week later, the same blue wax. The same shaking hand. One word under the first line: 'Please.'
plays.response: Let them; Corvane is big. The letter comes again a week later. Meanwhile the Sexton's sermon spreads south: two travelers at Kell's Crossing stop speaking. The Frost Tongue stays in his crown and the Concord needs Hieme, so tell the players plainly that this is where the winter bell is.
plays.consequence: Glassreach waits. The silence spreads down the North Road.
plays.fallback: If they waver, Edrin Moss offers to guide them for nothing: he wants to see what happens.
plays.tells: “We're not going to Glassreach.” Or the party plans another road.
plays.rules: The Tithe Clock resets once they have been out of Court cities for a week.
plays.later: Act IV: run whichever branch they reach first; Glassreach can follow. S15: with nobody to follow north, Isolde waits in Hallowmere. S22: without Hieme rung, the Concord is closed until they go north; the Second Dawn stays open.
plays.keywords: ignore, refuse, not going, skip, elsewhere, brassfall, vael tor, letter, hook, decline

plays.title: They leave Hallowmere tonight
plays.why: The letter says 'before the winter takes the last of me', and the Tithe Clock is ticking.
plays.readAloud: The city's lamps burn the same at midnight as at noon. Only the Hushmen change: fewer, colder, and more awake.
plays.response: Run Session 9 now, on the road. Ask the Hallowmere Ledger questions as they pass the gate. Anything left behind stays: Calla's Tongue on its shelf, Vaer silent, Jonah wherever he is. If they carry Calla's Tongue or the Ledger, the cart searches are still on (Gate Sweep); a night departure gives advantage on the group Stealth check.
plays.consequence: They are on the North Road with whatever they carried out.
plays.fallback: If they'd rather settle accounts first, play Session 9 in the city instead.
plays.tells: “We go now.” Players pack before the scene is over.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 13 at the north gate, with advantage at night.
plays.later: Act IV (Situation 21): Calla's Tongue is only in the Court's vault; coming back for it is a clear choice with a cost. S22: if Vaer and Calla are unrung, the Concord needs a return to Hallowmere, where a Silence Warrant or a tighter Tithe Clock may be waiting.
plays.keywords: leave, depart, tonight, go now, rush, north road, exit, flee city, hurry

plays.title: They ring Vaer
plays.why: They hold Vaer's Tongue and stand under the only thing in Hallowmere that isn't grey.
plays.readAloud: The bell cracks the grey like a knife through glass. For one heartbeat the cloud tears open, and a line of gold falls across the terraces. Every person in the city looks up. The opening widens. For this one day, sunlight reaches every terrace.
plays.response: First the silence-stone chains must come off: Rook's chain-key opens them, or DC 15 Thieves' Tools, or breaking three chain-stones (AC 12, 10 HP each), which is loud. Then state the Toll and wait for a yes: a memory of a dawn you loved; a Corvanese character raised in Hallowmere who never saw one may offer a memory of a hoped-for beginning instead. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. When it rings, the Court marks the Ringer with a Silence Warrant. If Sister Aurelie is in the city, she is on the terraces singing to Lathander within the hour, devoted to the party ever after, and arrested by dusk unless someone gets her out.
plays.consequence: Hallowmere has one real day of sun. The Ringer is wanted in every Court city.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer hesitates, Rook says, 'I've waited my whole life. I can wait one more minute.' And she does.
plays.tells: A player asks what Vaer would do, or what it costs.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (Toll, Vaer). Silence Warrant: any Hushman may arrest the Ringer on sight in a Court city; the Dawn Order enforces it only if Haldric won the duel. One day of true sunlight (Sunlight Sensitivity applies; dawn-based abilities at full strength).
plays.later: Concord: one more of six. S22: a freed Aurelie and her Dawn Mission are the Stormborn ally. S23: the Strike's Hushmen go for the Ringer first. Act V: Vaer's dawn lasts one day unless the final rite sustains it (Concord or Second Dawn).
plays.keywords: ring, vaer, dawn, bell, belfry, toll, sun, sunrise, warrant, chains, ringer

plays.title: They steal Vaer's Tongue from the armory
plays.why: Rook didn't win, or they don't want to owe her, and the armory is only a grille and a lock.
plays.readAloud: The armory is a long room of racked spears and dawn-yellow pennons gone grey. Behind an iron grille, a long bronze clapper hangs on a peg, the colour of sunlight in a country that has none.
plays.response: The grille's lock is DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with Thieves' Tools. Two Dawn Order knights guard the chain-room above, not the armory, so a quiet job never meets them unless the party climbs straight up to ring (Chain-Room Knights). If Ossa's Tongue was put here (S4), it hangs beside Vaer's: take both. Haldric checks the armory each dawn, so by the second hour the theft is known.
plays.consequence: The party holds Vaer's Tongue (and perhaps Ossa's), and the Dawn Order is hunting it.
plays.fallback: If the lock beats them, a young knight on night watch, a Rook loyalist, 'forgets' to lock the yard gate behind him.
plays.tells: Players ask where the armory is and who watches it.
plays.rules: Thieves' Tools DC 15. Stealth DC 13 through the barracks yard. Set Ossa's Tongue to 'With the party' if they take it too.
plays.later: S9: ring at once (past the chain-room knights) or carry it out past the gate searches. S23: if Haldric still holds his office, he rides with Maudrin to get it back.
plays.keywords: steal, vaer, tongue, armory, theft, grille, lock, dawn order, haldric, ossa

plays.title: They ring Calla at Kell's Crossing
plays.why: Calla's Tongue is in their pack and the Old Granary is on the North Road, three days out.
plays.readAloud: The sound is warm and round, and it smells of baking bread. The ash on the fields stirs. Somewhere a child laughs, and a woman begins to cry without knowing why. For one season, the grain comes up green across the plain.
plays.response: State the Toll and wait for a yes: a Gift, something the Ringer values, given freely to someone in need and never returned. Bet Ostrow is the natural recipient if she is with them; otherwise the innkeeper of the Empty Sheaf has six children and one coat. Nessa Harrow, Ila's mother, lives here: she comes out to look at the green fields, and if anyone says Ila's name, she sits down in the ash. Afterward, Court Tithe-men raid the Crossing for the rest of the season and try to capture the Ringer; play that out, don't assume it.
plays.consequence: One harvest season: bread for everyone. The Court's collectors are coming.
plays.fallback: If nobody wants to pay, Bet (if she remembers) asks to ring it herself; she has paid before.
plays.tells: The party stops at the fork, or asks what the Gift Toll means.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (Toll, Calla: Gift). At Kell's Crossing a character who gives a Gift gains Heroic Inspiration once per session. After ringing, decide where the Tongue goes: in the frame ('Left at the Old Granary') or on with the party.
plays.later: Concord: one more of six. S15: if they still carry Calla's Tongue, Isolde asks for it too. S28: Ila can meet her mother here, if anyone tells her.
plays.keywords: ring, calla, harvest, kell's crossing, granary, gift, toll, bread, bet, nessa harrow

plays.title: They smuggle a Tongue or a wanted Ringer past the gate
plays.why: Cart searches follow a vault theft for two days, and a Silence Warrant follows a Vaer ringing.
plays.readAloud: At the north gate four grey-gloved men are unloading every cart onto the road: grain sacks slit, barrels sounded, a coffin opened and closed again with an apology.
plays.response: Good routes: Bet's flour cart, which the Hushmen never search because she feeds them; Wren's Bellwright route through the Seaward Market drains (DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth) as a group, one wet hour); Ilam's roster, which names the shift whose Sergeant takes gold; Pass without Trace for a night crossing. Bluffing a search is DC 15 Charisma (Deception), +2 if Sergeant Cole remembers them from S4. Failure means the Gate Sweep encounter, never instant loss of the Tongue.
plays.consequence: They are out with what they carry, or they have a fight at the gate.
plays.fallback: If every plan fails, Captain Rook rides out of the gate 'on patrol' with the party in her escort, if she won the duel.
plays.tells: Players ask how carts leave the city, or who doesn't get searched.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 13. Deception DC 15. Pass without Trace (+10). A Tongue in a silence-stone-lined box doesn't hum, but the box itself is contraband.
plays.later: S15: if they fought their way out, Isolde's escort has two more Hushmen. S23: Maudrin knows exactly which Tongues they carry.
plays.keywords: smuggle, gate, search, cart, sneak out, hide tongue, escape city, bet's cart, drains, wren, warrant

plays.title: Isolde follows them north
plays.why: Isolde failed to keep them in the city; the Court sends her after them.
plays.readAloud: Two days out, a carriage with grey curtains stops at the same waystation you do. Nobody gets out. In the morning it is a mile behind you, and it stays a mile behind you.
plays.response: Isolde follows with two Hushmen (four if they fought their way out) to see what they find in the north. Spotting her is DC 15 Wisdom (Perception or Survival). They can confront her (she is charming and admits everything except her orders), lose her (Pass without Trace and a DC 15 group Survival check off the road), or ignore her. Losing her only delays her: she knows from the letter where they are going.
plays.consequence: The Court has eyes on the party all the way to Glassreach.
plays.fallback: If nobody looks back, Isolde sends a bottle of warm wine to their table at the second waystation, with her compliments.
plays.tells: The party notices the same carriage twice, or a player asks if they're being followed.
plays.rules: Perception or Survival DC 15 to notice. Group Survival DC 15 to lose her for two days.
plays.later: S15: Isolde arrives at the thaw with her escort; if they lost her, she arrives two days late, cold and angry, after the Spire is rung. If they capture her on the road, set her 'Captured', and the Court sends Tristan Vesk in her place.
plays.keywords: followed, tail, isolde, carriage, spy, chase, lose her, ambush, confront, north road

plays.title: They lie low until the searches stop
plays.why: Waiting out a two-day search is the sensible option, if the city lets them.
plays.readAloud: Two days of grey light through an attic window, and boots in the street below at odd hours. Bet brings up bread and doesn't ask.
plays.response: Two nights in Bet's attic, the Dawn Mission's cellar, or Rook's barracks. The cart searches end after two days. Each night is a Tithe Clock tick; at 6 the Court sweeps the city and puts a checkpoint on every road, which makes the wait self-defeating. Use the time: the Hallowmere Ledger questions, a last visit to Lysse, Ilam finding Jonah.
plays.consequence: The searches end. The Court's clock moves.
plays.fallback: If the clock is already near 6, Bet says plainly, 'You can't stay. They're counting.'
plays.tells: “We hide for a couple of days.”
plays.rules: Tithe Clock +2. At 6: Hushmen sweep, checkpoints on every road (Gate Sweep at every gate).
plays.later: S10: the Tithe Clock resets after a week outside Court cities. If it hits 12 before they leave, silence-stones go into every street; they stay even after the party is gone, waiting for any return in Act IV.
plays.keywords: hide, lie low, wait, rest, attic, safe house, searches, delay, tithe clock

plays.title: They go back to Pellmoor before heading north
plays.why: Ila, Ossa's bell, Venn's export trade or Aurelie's mission pull some tables back to the Mere before Glassreach.
plays.readAloud: The Quays are louder than you remember. Forty masts, no gulls, and on the Tally's slate the day's rate: 1 KEEP = 1 GP 2 SP. Someone has chalked underneath it: HOW MUCH FOR A MOTHER?
plays.response: Pellmoor is three days by ferry and road, and Glassreach is then about two weeks away. With Ossa's Tongue back in hand, the Tidewarden ferries the Ringer to the Ossa Belfry (S3, Scene 4); Water Breathing or his air pocket gets them down. Venn's counting-house holds the other half of the EXPORT column, and confronting him in public makes him their enemy and moves the Landing. Reckoner Sela Maunt can tell exported keeps by their wax stamps, and her Lost Shelf may hold a heartkeep they have been looking for.
plays.consequence: The north waits. Pellmoor's threads tighten.
plays.fallback: If the detour stalls, Brannagh Wick tells them the Seam is narrowing for the season and Venn's last ship sails in four days.
plays.tells: Players talk about Ila, Venn, or ringing Ossa with a recovered Tongue.
plays.rules: Ossa's Toll: a memory of someone who has died. Water Breathing (3rd level); holding breath lasts 1 + Constitution modifier minutes. Set Venn to 'Exposed, now hostile' if they confront him publicly.
plays.later: S22: the Stormborn ally (Harper agents, the Dawn Mission, or a Baldurian crew) is earned here if they exposed Venn or protected the ferry-folk. S15: Isolde follows them to Pellmoor and north again; only the days change.
plays.keywords: pellmoor, return, detour, ila, venn, export, ossa, ring ossa, tidewarden, sela maunt, aurelie, mere

plays.title: They settle accounts before the road
plays.why: Every Act II choice needs to be on record before Act III, and the players enjoy the recap.
plays.readAloud: The North Road runs up out of the city between grey hedges, and the Dawn Order's watchtower falls behind you. Ahead, the land rises toward the Ninefold hills. Somewhere behind, a single bell tolls once, muffled by the cloud, and then falls silent.
plays.response: Ask the seven Hallowmere Ledger questions aloud and let the players answer: the jar, Rook or Haldric, Jonah and Ilam, Maudrin's bargain, the diary, the Tongues, Tessa. Set the matching flags in Foresight as they answer. Then ask which unfinished promise they carry north, and write it as a Bargain Log line.
plays.consequence: Your state is correct before Act III.
plays.fallback: If the players don't remember something, it didn't happen; don't punish a forgotten thread.
plays.tells: The party reaches the north gate, or asks 'What did we leave undone?'
plays.rules: Level the party to 5 once Hallowmere is resolved.
plays.later: Every answer is a later: S15 (Isolde, Tongues carried), S22 (allies: Dawn Order, Blanks, Ilam), S23 (Haldric present or absent, Jonah hostage or safe, Maudrin's favor).
plays.keywords: recap, summary, ledger, promises, questions, leave city, north road, level up, unfinished

plays.title: They push into the glass without proper gear
plays.why: Parties rarely pack for a winter that has lasted four hundred years.
plays.readAloud: The cold here doesn't bite. It waits. After an hour your fingers stop telling you where they are, and your breath falls from your mouth as tiny stars that ring when they hit the ground.
plays.response: Glassreach is Extreme Cold. At the end of each hour, each creature makes a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gains 1 Exhaustion level; Resistance or Immunity to Cold damage means automatic success, and so does a warm cloak or other cold-weather gear (house rule kept from v5). Each Exhaustion level is −2 to every d20 Test and −5 feet of Speed; a long rest removes one. Yara sells warm cloaks at her camp for 10 gp or a keep each, or trades one for a good tool. Telegraph it: the first failed save is a character's hands going white.
plays.consequence: Gear matters, and so does Yara.
plays.fallback: If a player is sliding toward a third level, Yara throws a cloak at them and puts it on their tab.
plays.tells: Nobody mentions cloaks, or a player asks how cold it really is.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold (DMG 2024): DC 10 Constitution save hourly or 1 Exhaustion level. Warm cloak or Cold Resistance: automatic success. Exhaustion: −2 per level to d20 Tests, −5 ft Speed; long rest removes 1.
plays.later: S11–S14: every hour in the glass is another save for anyone without a cloak; climbing the Spire at two Exhaustion levels is −4 on each Athletics check. S15: the woken Stilled need cloaks too.
plays.keywords: cold, extreme cold, freeze, freezing, exhaustion, warm cloak, gear, frostbite, constitution, winter, glassreach

plays.title: They befriend Yara Thenn
plays.why: She sells what they need, knows every safe path, and is funny.
plays.readAloud: “I'll tell you where the safe paths are. You tell me why you're going to the Sexton. Nobody goes to the Sexton for a pleasant chat. And if you're going to die, I'd like to know what for, so I can sell the story.”
plays.response: Yara sells glass-cutting tools (5 gp), warm cloaks and maps; she haggles constantly and prefers favours or good tools to coin. Befriending her needs honesty about the Sexton (Influence DC 15, with advantage if they tell her the truth). Friendly, she gives them the map of safe paths: advantage on Survival in Glassreach and no wandering Glass-Wolves on the marked paths. What she wants most is a map of the Frost Spire, because nobody has ever drawn one.
plays.consequence: The party has safe paths and a guide who will come as far as the Stilled Clearing.
plays.fallback: If they insult her, she still sells them cloaks, at double price, and the map stays in her pocket.
plays.tells: Players haggle, joke back, or ask about the Sexton.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Yara starts Indifferent). Survival with her map: advantage.
plays.later: S14: a sketch of the Spire brought back to her earns her loyalty and the second ice stair (one fewer climbing check). S15: she knows how to feed and warm the waking Stilled. S30: Yara finally opens her brother's glass-flower.
plays.keywords: yara, thenn, scavenger, camp, map, safe paths, guide, haggle, buy, tools, cloaks

plays.title: They ask about the flower Yara won't sell
plays.why: Players notice the one thing a merchant refuses to price.
plays.readAloud: It sits in a felt-lined box: a single glass rose, and inside it something moves like a laugh caught in a jar. “That's not for sale,” Yara says, and shuts the box before you can see the colour.
plays.response: It holds a moment of her dead brother Teo's laugh, and she has never opened it because she is afraid it will shatter. It cannot be bought or stolen: if anyone tries, she closes the camp to them. If someone shares a true memory of their own grief with her, freely, she tells them about Teo and the winter that took him, and the giver earns Heroic Inspiration. A Bell-Touched character can tell her it will not shatter; that is true, and she does not believe it yet.
plays.consequence: Yara trusts them with the one thing she owns that matters.
plays.fallback: If they push, she says, 'Some things you keep because you can't afford what they cost,' and changes the subject to cloaks.
plays.tells: A player asks to buy it, or asks why she keeps it.
plays.rules: Heroic Inspiration for a memory given freely to someone who needs it (v6 generosity rule).
plays.later: S15: as the thaw spreads, glass-flowers soften, and Yara has to decide whether to open hers before it melts. S30: she opens it.
plays.keywords: glass-flower, flower, rose, brother, teo, laugh, not for sale, yara, buy, steal, grief

plays.title: They free the Stilled child
plays.why: A frozen child in a clearing is the clearest call to act in the forest.
plays.readAloud: “The man in the tower was sad. He sang to us so we wouldn't be afraid. Then he stopped singing, and the winter kept going, and we couldn't move anymore. Is it still winter out there?”
plays.response: The deer, the fox and the child stand mid-step in the Stilled Clearing. Cutting her free with glass-cutting tools is DC 12 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) and harms nothing; smashing it is DC 15 Strength and sends cracks into the deer and fox, which shatter and die. Any fire or lightning attack at the glass melts it safely in one round. She wakes, says her one true sentence, and freezes again within a minute; she does not attack. If child peril is a Line at your table, she is an old woman who was a child when the winter came.
plays.consequence: They know the Sexton once sang to the Stilled, and that the winter kept going when he stopped.
plays.fallback: If they won't touch her, Wyn Talla asks them to, because her sister is three trees away and she needs to know it can be done.
plays.tells: A player kneels by the child, or asks whether she is alive.
plays.rules: Sleight of Hand DC 12 with glass-cutting tools, or Strength DC 15 to smash. Fire or lightning damage at the glass melts it.
plays.later: S12: 'The man in the tower was sad' tells them he can be talked to. S15: after Hieme rings, she is among the first to wake for good, and she asks for her mother.
plays.keywords: child, stilled child, girl, wake, free, break glass, cut, clearing, deer, fox, frozen

plays.title: A Faerûnian character recognises a Stilled sailor
plays.why: Some of the Stilled are Sword Coast sailors from before the Quiet Night, and a Stormborn character will know the cut of their coats.
plays.readAloud: Among the Stilled at the clearing's edge stands a man in a sea-coat cut four hundred years out of fashion, a brass badge on his breast: a ship under three stars, the old arms of a Tethyrian merchant house.
plays.response: A Sword Coast character recognises the badge with a DC 10 Intelligence (History) check; a sailor knows it outright. He is Bosun Corran Vell of the carrack Brightwater, out of Zazesspur, Stilled in 2 SS. Melted gently (fire at the glass, or Yara's tools), he wakes Hostile from shock but not violent at once; Influence DC 15 in Common calms him. He speaks an old dialect of Common, asks what year it is ('Is it still ten hundred and eighty-two?'), and says the Brightwater's crew are somewhere in these trees.
plays.consequence: The Stilled include Faerûnians. Someone from the Sword Coast came looking for the Ringing Land four centuries ago and never went home.
plays.fallback: If no one is Faerûnian, Yara points at the badge: 'Loudfolk. Old ones. There's a dozen of them by the stream.'
plays.tells: A Faerûnian or a sailor looks closely at the Stilled at the clearing's edge.
plays.rules: History DC 10. Influence DC 15 (Indifferent after a calm word). Comprehend Languages or Tongues helps with the old dialect, but any Common speaker gets the gist.
plays.later: S15: the Brightwater's crew wake with the thaw and want passage home through the Seam; getting them to Pellmoor earns a Stormborn ally for S22. S11: if not woken gently, Vell is one of the Stilled in the ambush.
plays.keywords: faerunian, stormborn, sailor, tethyr, zazesspur, badge, ship, brightwater, corran vell, old common, sword coast, year

plays.title: They leave the safe paths or split up
plays.why: The forest is beautiful, the Spire is visible, and the shortest line is never the safe one.
plays.readAloud: A crack like a whip, somewhere to your left. Then a howl that rings, high and pure, the way a wineglass does when you run a wet finger round its rim.
plays.response: Off Yara's paths the glass is thin and the Glass-Wolves hunt by sound. Telegraph first with the crack and the howl, then run Off the Path: every wolf that shatters cracks the glass around nearby Stilled, and two of them wake. If the party split, cut between the groups and bring them together at the Stilled Clearing when the howling starts.
plays.consequence: The wolves are a warning; the woken Stilled are the real cost.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly, Yara's whistle from the path draws the wolves off; glass-wolves hate a high, steady note.
plays.tells: A player cuts across the glass, or the party splits to cover more ground.
plays.rules: Survival DC 14 to keep to a path without Yara's map. Extreme Cold saves continue through the fight.
plays.later: S11: the two Stilled who woke angry remember who cracked them, and the ambush has two fewer sleepers in it. S15: Stilled harmed now are slower to trust.
plays.keywords: off path, shortcut, split up, wander, explore, wolves, glass-wolves, lost, separate, scout ahead

plays.title: They use fire, Shatter or Thunderwave in the glass
plays.why: Level-5 casters have Fireball, and a forest of glass looks like a problem fire solves.
plays.readAloud: Yara grabs your wrist before the last word. “Not here. Not near them. You don't know what's inside the glass.”
plays.response: Be firm and say it before they cast: fire and lightning melt winter-moments, thunder shatters them. A Fireball in the clearing melts the glass around every Stilled in its area at once: the animals die, adults wake Hostile and in pain (they take the damage), and the child wakes and runs. Shatter or Thunderwave on a Stilled's glass breaks it with the person inside, who takes the damage and wakes screaming. Every spell hums, so Yara hears it coming.
plays.consequence: Magic can wake the whole forest at once, but not gently.
plays.fallback: If they cast anyway, the waking adults run before they fight; give the party one round to choose calm or steel.
plays.tells: A caster asks what fire does to the glass, or starts the incantation.
plays.rules: Fire or lightning damage to a winter-moment melts it; thunder damage shatters it and the Stilled inside takes the damage. Tell the player before they commit.
plays.later: S11: an early Stilled Ambush. S15: the Stilled remember who woke them with fire, and their trust comes slower.
plays.keywords: fireball, fire, burn, melt, shatter, thunderwave, thunder, spell, glass, area spell, explode

plays.title: A character sees themselves in the glass
plays.why: This is the seed v5 plants for Act V; it happens to someone whether they look for it or not.
plays.readAloud: In a sheet of glass as tall as a door you see yourself. Older. Grey at the temples. Holding a small dark key in both hands, and smiling.
plays.response: Choose the character whose story is most tied to the bells, or the player who looked first. Do not explain it. Ask the player, “What does your character feel?” and write the answer down word for word. If they break the glass, every shard shows the same thing.
plays.consequence: A seed for Act V. Nothing changes now.
plays.fallback: If nobody looks, the glass shows it to the character on watch that night.
plays.tells: A player looks into a tall sheet of glass, or lingers alone.
plays.rules: No roll. Detect Magic shows nothing: it is not a spell.
plays.later: S26: the same figure stands at the foot of Ysh, older, holding the Key and smiling; read back what the player said here. S27: whether it was the Concord's Ringer or something else is the player's to decide.
plays.keywords: vision, reflection, glass, older self, key, smiling, mirror, future, winter-moment, h-18

plays.title: They damage the glass around a Stilled adult
plays.why: Waking the child worked; players try the same on the adults, or crack one by accident.
plays.readAloud: A crack runs up the glass like frost on a window. Inside, an eye moves. Then a hand. The man inside is screaming, and you cannot hear it until the glass breaks.
plays.response: Waking in pain and terror, an adult attacks whoever is closest, and the noise cracks the glass of others. Run the Stilled Ambush: they wake one or two a round, not all at once, so the party can see it growing and leave. A Stilled child does not attack; she speaks once and freezes again unless threatened. A Stilled who is spoken to mid-fight (Influence DC 15 as an action, in Hesk or old Common) stops, shaking, and becomes Indifferent.
plays.consequence: Some Stilled are hurt or broken; some may be calmed.
plays.fallback: If the fight turns grim, Maren Talla (if awake) stands in front of the next one and says its name.
plays.tells: A hammer raised to an adult's glass, or a fight near the Stilled.
plays.rules: Stilled Person (Gargoyle base): slow to start, hard to hurt through glass. Influence DC 15 as an action to calm one.
plays.later: S15: Stilled who were calmed rather than shattered are the first to trust the party. S22: the Stilled walk to the Tor only if that trust is earned.
plays.keywords: crack, break, hammer, wake, stilled, adult, ambush, attack, glass, fight

plays.title: They wake a Stilled adult slowly and kindly
plays.why: Wyn Talla wants her sister freed, and patient tables look for a way that isn't a hammer.
plays.readAloud: You wrap the glass in two cloaks and wait. It takes an hour. Water runs down the inside like tears, and then Maren Talla takes her first breath in three hundred and eighty years.
plays.response: Melting with warmth over an hour (cloaks, a campfire, a held Produce Flame) or with glass-cutting tools (DC 12 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand)) wakes a Stilled without pain. They wake confused and Indifferent, not hostile; give them a name to hear and they listen. Maren asks for Wyn, who is now an old woman, and both of them weep. Maren knows one useful thing: the Sexton's chapel is past the second frozen stream, and he cannot bear to be argued with.
plays.consequence: One Stilled is free and grateful. Wyn has her sister back.
plays.fallback: If nobody has the patience, Wyn sits down by the glass to do it herself, and the party has to decide whether to leave her there.
plays.tells: Players ask whether warmth or time would do it.
plays.rules: An hour of warmth. Rescuers who gave up their cloaks make Extreme Cold saves. Sleight of Hand DC 12 with tools.
plays.later: S12–S13: Maren's warning gives the party a free chance to stop arguing before the glass cracks. S15: Maren and Wyn lead the waking Stilled to Yara's camp, which counts toward the Stilled's trust.
plays.keywords: gentle, melt, warm, slow, wake, maren, wyn, talla, sister, kind, careful, produce flame

plays.title: They slip past the Stilled without waking them
plays.why: Stealthy parties avoid fights with victims.
plays.readAloud: You move between the frozen people like guests at a sleeping house. A wolf lifts its glass head somewhere in the trees, listens, and lowers it again.
plays.response: The Stilled act only when glass cracks; the Glass-Wolves are the danger. A group DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth) check gets everyone through; Yara's map gives advantage and Pass without Trace gives +10. On a failure, one wolf's howl cracks one Stilled's glass: a single adult wakes, not the full ambush, and the party can still leave.
plays.consequence: No fight, and no Stilled harmed.
plays.fallback: If they fail, describe the single waking adult as confused first and angry second, and let them choose.
plays.tells: Players ask which paths avoid the clearing, or cast Pass without Trace.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 13; advantage with Yara's map; Pass without Trace +10.
plays.later: S14: the Spire's guard pack is the same pack; if it never saw them, the party has surprise at the Spire.
plays.keywords: sneak, stealth, avoid, slip past, pass without trace, quiet, careful, bypass

plays.title: They shatter Stilled or question the dead ones
plays.why: Treating the Stilled as monsters is quick, and a cleric with Speak with Dead wants answers.
plays.readAloud: The glass comes apart in a sound like a chandelier falling. What was inside does not get up.
plays.response: Shattering a Stilled kills it; there is no reforming. Say so plainly the first time. Speak with Dead works on a shattered Stilled, since it is dead now: it remembers 2 SS, the first night of the winter, and a man in a tower singing so nobody would be afraid.
