plays.why: Corin's whole family has tried to finish this song for three generations.
plays.readAloud: "It's the only way to end it, not just hold it. My grandmother died one breath into this song. Let me finish it."
plays.response: He knows the Ringer pays all six Tolls; he believes everyone risking the world is acceptable. He is wrong, not evil. Let the party argue it out. He can defer a Toll for an hour, never cancel it.
plays.consequence: The party's stance on the Unbound is clear before the Tor.
plays.tells: Corin is allied and reads the Notes with the party.
plays.later: S26: if the party refuses him, Corin may try the strike himself if he reaches the bell with the Key; treat him like Maudrin's threat, interruptible.
plays.keywords: corin, strike, ring the seventh, bellwright, argue, wake oum

plays.title: They ambush Maudrin's column on the road
plays.why: Proactive parties strike first, on ground they choose.
plays.readAloud: From the ridge you can see the column coming: grey horses, grey gloves, and one rider in dove-grey at the centre.
plays.response: Ansel knows the routes Maudrin's Hushmen take from the palace to the Tor. A good ambush gives the party Surprise and a chosen battlefield; run the Strike there instead of at the Tor's foot.
plays.consequence: The Strike happens on the party's terms.
plays.tells: Players ask Ansel Quay or a scout for her route.
plays.rules: Surprise (2024): surprised creatures have Disadvantage on their Initiative rolls. Group Stealth: DC 14 against the column's Passive Perception.
plays.later: S23 as normal, with terrain and surprise in the party's favour.
plays.keywords: ambush, road, column, attack first, ansel, route, surprise

plays.title: Maudrin calls in the Session 4 favor
plays.why: If the party accepted her bargain at the Assembly, she collects now.
plays.readAloud: "One favor, dear, and I am calling it in now. Go, before I change my mind."
plays.response: She asks them to stand aside. If they do, the Strike doesn't happen and she reaches the Tor ahead of them. If they refuse, the favor is broken and the Strike begins; she remembers.
plays.consequence: The party honours a promise to the antagonist, or breaks it.
plays.tells: The Bargain log shows the favor still owed.
plays.rules: Record the favor as Kept or Broken in the Bargain log.
plays.later: Kept: S24 she reaches the summit unhurt with all her forces. Broken: she offers no more bargains, only threats.
plays.keywords: favor, maudrin, bargain, owe, called in, stand aside, go

plays.title: They fight the Strike
plays.why: Most parties won't give up the Tongues.
plays.readAloud: Hushmen on grey horses come over the ridge in a long line. Their gloves catch the light and throw it back as silence. Behind them rides a figure in dove-grey. "Good evening," Maudrin Vesk says. "I'm so sorry to interrupt. But I believe you have something that belongs to me."
plays.response: Run the Strike. She wants the Tongues the party carries and the Key back if they hold it. She retreats toward the Tor when Bloodied: "I'll see you at the Shrine." Track her HP and the Key's possession into the next scene. Each ally's one action applies.
plays.consequence: The Court's army is broken or holds the road.
plays.fallback: If the fight turns, the allies' actions (riders, the Stilled, the Choir) are the cavalry.
plays.tells: Weapons out on the ridge; the party refuses her offer.
plays.rules: Encounter: the Strike (pick the version for the oath-duel's result). 2024 difficulty is shown for your roster.
plays.later: S24: Maudrin at the summit with whatever HP she has left. Level 10 after the Strike.
plays.keywords: fight, strike, battle, ridge, maudrin, hushmen, army, combat

plays.title: They surrender to Maudrin
plays.why: Outnumbered parties sometimes yield.
plays.readAloud: "Thank you. That was wise. Now: the Tongues, please. And your Ringer will come with me to the Quiet Court."
plays.response: She takes the Tongues, and the Key if the party holds it. She demands the party's Ringer come to be Tithed; the player chooses whether to accept. A saving throw never decides consent. Refusal leads to negotiation, escape or a capture attempt. Use the Empty Choir only if the group accepts this as the end of its resistance; otherwise play rescue or escape.
plays.consequence: The Court holds the Tongues and the Key.
plays.fallback: Offer an escape: Brannagh's pilots, Yenna's riders, or a Stormborn ship waiting off the coast.
plays.tells: Players ask her terms.
plays.later: Forecast: the Empty Choir comes into play; a rescue chapter can reverse it.
plays.keywords: surrender, give up, yield, hand over tongues, captured, terms

plays.title: The Key in the party's hands breaks the Court's line
plays.why: Haldric didn't know the Key was real until he sees it.
plays.readAloud: Ser Haldric Mose sees the grey case in your hands and stops, sword half raised, like a man who has just heard his own name spoken in a language he never learned.
plays.response: Haldric loses his next turn. His knights look to him and hesitate too. The Court's line breaks; Hushmen fall back to Maudrin.
plays.consequence: The Strike turns in the party's favour.
plays.tells: The party takes the Key mid-fight and Haldric is present.
plays.rules: Haldric and the Dawn Order Knights lose their next turns.
plays.later: S24: Haldric may be turned by the truth of his parentage.
plays.keywords: haldric, hesitate, key, line breaks, knights, court

plays.title: Maudrin holds Jonah as a hostage
plays.why: If the party left Jonah in Court custody (S7), she brings him to the ridge.
plays.readAloud: A Hushman lifts a thin boy onto his saddle. He is holding a wooden bird.
plays.response: Freeing Jonah costs one Tongue, or winning the Strike. Use your session-zero boundaries for child peril; if it's a Line, make him an adult dependent or remove the threat. If Ilam is an ally, he goes for his son without being asked.
plays.consequence: A Tongue for a child, or a fight for him.
plays.tells: Jonah is in custody in World state.
plays.later: S28–30: Jonah remembers his mother's face if she is found.
plays.keywords: jonah, hostage, child, wooden bird, ilam, rescue, trade

plays.title: Ilam Bray holds the southern road
plays.why: If Ilam and Jonah were reunited, Ilam has his own reasons to be here.
plays.readAloud: Ilam Bray stands in the road with his grey gloves off. Behind him, Jonah holds the wooden bird in both hands and watches his father, and knows him.
plays.response: Ilam stays between the boy and the fight and holds the southern road: the Court's reinforcements don't reach the ridge. Give Jonah one quiet moment of recognition.
plays.consequence: The Strike is smaller; a family is whole.
plays.tells: Ilam is an ally in World state.
plays.rules: Remove two Hushmen from the Strike.
plays.later: S29: Ilam stays with his son.
plays.keywords: ilam, jonah, road, father, son, ally, hold

plays.title: They fight Maudrin at the summit
plays.why: She still holds the Key and stands between the party and the stairs.
plays.readAloud: "I'm glad you came," Maudrin says. "Shall we begin?" Behind her the Hush rises out of the stairway like a tide, so low you feel it in your ribs.
plays.response: Run the summit. Maudrin fights to slow the party and retreats down the stairs when Bloodied; she means to seal the Key and keep her rule. Before she can act at the bell, establish her threat aloud: if they are about to take the Key, she will strike rather than lose control. Allies from Session 22 take one action each.
plays.consequence: Maudrin is beaten back down the stairs, or captured, or the party holds the Key.
plays.fallback: If the fight turns against the party, an ally's one dramatic action (the Stilled, Yenna's riders, the Cantor's hymn) opens a way past.
plays.tells: Weapons out at the stone ring; casters ready Counterspell.
plays.rules: Encounter: the summit. Carry her actual HP into Session 26. Her Warden's Retreat is a Bonus Action once Bloodied. Grapple and disarm work by 2024 rules; the Key's case can be taken (DC 16 Sleight of Hand once she has been hit).
plays.later: S25: the stairs. S26: if she reaches the bell with the Key, she is at the bell with whatever HP she had left.
plays.keywords: fight, maudrin, summit, battle, attack, final battle, tor

plays.title: They take the Key from Maudrin at the summit
plays.why: A good grapple or a nimble rogue ends the race to the bell before it starts.
plays.readAloud: The case comes away in your hand, heavier than it looks, humming through the silence-stone like a heart through a wall.
plays.response: Once she has been struck this fight, a character who reaches her can take the case. On a success Maudrin stops fighting: she has nothing left to bargain with and knows it. On a failure she notices and keeps it; she escapes only by ordinary movement.
plays.consequence: The party holds the Key at the top of the stairs.
plays.tells: A player positions next to her and asks about the chain.
plays.rules: DC 16 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), or win a grapple and use an action to take it.
plays.later: Forecast: Concord, Second Dawn and the Unbound now depend only on the party. S26 runs the party-holds-the-Key version.
plays.keywords: take the key, steal, grab, case, chain, sleight of hand, summit

plays.title: They talk with Maudrin instead of fighting
plays.why: If the party already holds the Key, she negotiates; even if not, she always offers words first.
plays.readAloud: "I'm not your enemy. I'm the last person in Corvane who understands what the silence costs. Four centuries of Tithes. Blanks. Children who forget their mothers. And you want to wake the thing that holds it all together? You're mad, or you're brave. I've never been able to tell the difference."
plays.response: Let her make her case honestly: she has kept the lullaby steady for thirty-eight years by keeping the truth from everyone. She will agree to a seal if she thinks the party won't strike. She makes her Final Offer (H-26): everything they want, all of it already Tithed and in her vault. She can be persuaded to surrender, or to come down the stairs as a witness.
plays.consequence: A truce at the summit, on terms.
plays.fallback: If talk breaks down, she retreats down the stairs rather than fight a party that holds the Key.
plays.tells: Someone lowers a weapon and asks her why.
plays.rules: Influence (Persuasion) DC 17 while she holds the Key; automatic if the party holds the Key and offers her a seal. Insight DC 15: she believes every word.
plays.later: S26: she may stand beside the bell weeping rather than fighting. S27: she can argue for her vision with Oum but never decides for the table. Optional variant: she offers to pay the Great Toll herself (Concord with her as the Seventh's voice), only with the party's agreement.
plays.keywords: talk, negotiate, maudrin, persuade, surrender, final offer, parley

plays.title: They capture Maudrin
plays.why: Some parties want her alive to answer for the Tithe.
plays.readAloud: She sits down on the cold stone very carefully, like an old woman at the end of a long day, and holds out her wrists.
plays.response: A creature reduced to 0 HP by a melee attack can be knocked out instead of killed (2024). Bound, she talks: the diary, the Key, the lullaby. Her Hushmen surrender if she orders it. Haldric, if present and told she is his mother, takes her into custody himself.
plays.consequence: Maudrin is a prisoner; the Court is leaderless.
plays.tells: Players announce non-lethal blows or ask about manacles and silence-stone.
plays.rules: Non-lethal: declare when the melee attack drops her to 0 HP.
plays.later: S29: her fate is the party's to decide: trial, exile, or Tithe by her own office. Tristan Vesk moves to fill her chair.
plays.keywords: capture, knock out, non-lethal, prisoner, arrest maudrin, spare

plays.title: They kill Maudrin
plays.why: Thirty-eight years of Tithes makes her an easy villain to finish.
plays.readAloud: The silence-stone gloves fall open. For the first time since you met her, Maudrin Vesk makes a sound: one breath out, very long, like someone setting down something heavy.
plays.response: She dies. If she held the Key, it is on her body. Her Hushmen scatter or surrender. If Haldric is present and knew she was his mother, he takes her body down the hill and does not come back.
plays.consequence: The Chancellor is dead; the Key is free.
plays.tells: No one declares mercy; someone asks whether she's still breathing.
plays.later: S29: Tristan Vesk becomes Chancellor and wants the Key. S28–30: Haldric learns the truth from her letters (v5).
plays.keywords: kill maudrin, death, execute, finish her, dead

plays.title: They tell Haldric he is Maudrin's son
plays.why: If they found proof (her diary, Isolde's secrets, Ansel's files), this is the moment.
plays.readAloud: Haldric stops polishing his sword. He looks at Maudrin, and she does not deny it, and that is worse than anything she could have said.
plays.response: Haldric half-suspected it. Faced with proof and her silence, he lowers his sword and steps out of the Court's line. He won't fight her, and he won't fight for her.
plays.consequence: Haldric and any knights loyal to him leave the fight.
plays.tells: Players have evidence and Haldric is on the field.
plays.rules: Evidence makes it automatic; without it, Influence (Persuasion) DC 18.
plays.later: S29: Haldric chooses his own fate, possibly the Dawn Order's captaincy under Rook.
plays.keywords: haldric, son, mother, maudrin, truth, reveal, parentage

plays.title: They descend the stairs of the Hush
plays.why: The bell is at the bottom of a hundred steps.
plays.readAloud: The stairs go on for a long time. Each step has a memory carved into it, worn smooth by the feet of those who came to listen. Some are your memories. Some are strangers'. You hear a child laughing, a bell tolling, a man telling a joke to someone who isn't there.
plays.response: Disclose the full price at the first step: every descender loses memories as they go. Each makes one save at the entrance; five memories on a failure, two on a success, once per character for the whole campaign, including earlier visits. Players may turn back. Each names their losses briefly, or keeps a private list and shares one. Losses are recollections, never class features, player knowledge or control of the character.
plays.consequence: The descenders reach Ysh, lighter.
plays.fallback: If the price stops the table cold, offer the foundry chute (next play).
plays.tells: Players ask who goes down and who stays.
plays.rules: DC 13 Wisdom saving throw at the entrance. Record each loss as Stairs in the Memory ledger.
plays.later: S26: who stands at the bell is who paid the stairs. These losses are not Tolls and are not refunded by any ending.
plays.keywords: stairs, descend, hush, memories, cost, walk down, hundred steps

plays.title: They find another way down
plays.why: v5 says a route that genuinely avoids the stairs avoids their price.
plays.readAloud: At the top of the Tor, under the ring of stones, the old casting-pit drops straight down into the dark. Warm air rises out of it, smelling of bronze.
plays.response: The bells were cast at the summit and lowered to their halls; the casting chute still drops to the Hush chamber. It's a hard climb in the dark but costs no memories. Corin or the Notes can point it out. Flight or teleportation that reaches the chamber also works. Don't add a replacement punishment.
plays.consequence: The party reaches the bell with every memory intact.
plays.tells: Players ask about the old foundry where the bells were cast, or prepare flight or Dimension Door.
plays.rules: Three DC 15 Strength (Athletics) checks to climb; a failure is a slip: 2024 Falling, 1d6 Bludgeoning per 10 feet fallen (decide the distance before rolling, usually 20 feet).
plays.later: S26 as normal. Allies who can't climb wait above.
plays.keywords: another way, avoid stairs, foundry, chute, climb, fly, dimension door, shortcut

plays.title: Allies refuse to go down
plays.why: Some NPCs will not pay with their memories, and some will, which is the beat.
plays.readAloud: Ilam Bray looks down the stairs for a long moment, then at Jonah. "I've only just got him back," he says. "I can't lose him again."
plays.response: Let the allies choose in character. Those who stay hold the summit. Those who go pay the stairs like anyone else. Never make an absent player's character pay.
plays.consequence: The party knows who is with them all the way down.
plays.tells: Players turn to Ila, Rook, Yenna or Ilam at the top step.
plays.later: S28–30: an ally who paid the stairs carries that in their epilogue.
plays.keywords: allies, refuse, stay behind, ila, ilam, rook, yenna, go down, companions

plays.title: They stop Maudrin striking Ysh
plays.why: If she holds the Key at the bell, the whole world hangs on one action.
plays.readAloud: Maudrin stands beside the bell with the Key raised. "Let me seal it, and the world continues. Take another step, and I will choose what follows." Her hand is shaking.
plays.response: Ask what the characters do before she acts; if combat begins, roll initiative. Striking needs her action while adjacent to Ysh with the Key out of its case. Grappling, disarming, bargaining and blocking her route can all prevent it. She prefers a negotiated seal and Court custody of the Key. Only a completed strike opens the Unbound; killing her afterward can't undo the sound.
plays.consequence: She strikes, seals, surrenders, or loses the Key.
plays.fallback: If the table freezes, have her hesitate one heartbeat and say a name: Cassia's, or her grandmother Ilse's.
plays.tells: Maudrin raises the Key; players shout, move, or reach for a spell.
plays.rules: Initiative; her strike is her action on her turn. Grapple (2024 Unarmed Strike option) or disarm. Counterspell can't stop it: the strike is not a spell.
plays.later: Struck: S27 runs the Unbound (Remake or Unmake, the players decide). Sealed by her: the Empty Choir only if the group ends its resistance.
plays.keywords: strike, stop her, maudrin, bell, ysh, grapple, disarm, prevent, block

plays.title: Maudrin strikes the Seventh
plays.why: If no one stops her action, she chooses what follows.
plays.readAloud: The Hush cracks. The lullaby falls silent, and the world goes quiet in a way you have never heard before: not the silence of the bells, but the silence of a held breath about to be released.
plays.response: She pays all six Tolls. Oum opens an eye. The players, not Maudrin and not the DM, choose Remake or Unmake through their conversation with Oum (S27).
plays.consequence: Ysh is struck. Oum wakes.
plays.tells: She is adjacent to Ysh with the Key uncased on her turn.
plays.later: S27: the Unbound. Unmake needs everyone's agreement; otherwise Remake, with each player naming something preserved.
plays.keywords: strike, maudrin strikes, bell rings, oum wakes, unbound

plays.title: The party stands at the bell with the Key
plays.why: Everything ends here, and the party decides.
plays.readAloud: The bell is vast and blank, its surface like the face of a sleeping god. You stand before it with the Key in your hands. The lullaby is still there, very faint, asking you to be quiet. Your choice is the only one left in the world.
plays.response: The figure from the Session 11 winter-moment stands at the bell's foot: the character, older, holding the Key, smiling. Ask that player what they feel; don't explain. Then disclose every option and its price before anyone acts (Forecast tab lists which are open): Concord, Unbound, Second Dawn. Take a table break before an irreversible choice.
plays.consequence: The campaign's ending is chosen.
plays.fallback: If the table can't agree, they may postpone: leave with the Key, unsealed, and keep adventuring.
plays.tells: The party holds the Key at the bottom of the stairs.
plays.rules: Concord: seat the Key without striking, a willing Ringer accepts the Great Toll (ask in private). Unbound: strike, the striker pays all six Tolls. Second Dawn: one uninterrupted minute to seal the Key in its recess, no Toll.
plays.later: S27 resolves the chosen path. S28–30 epilogues follow the ring ledger.
plays.keywords: choice, key, bell, ysh, ending, decide, seventh, final choice

plays.title: They perform the Concord
plays.why: Every regional bell rang; the Key is theirs; one person is willing.
plays.readAloud: You hear the six bells, each in its own voice: the dawn bell's clean light, the memory-bell's deep sorrow, the frost-bell's thin ice, the harvest's warm round sound, the storm's crack, the dream's soft lullaby. Together they form a chord that has not existed for four centuries. The chord rises and wraps around the Hush.
plays.response: Ask the Ringer's player in private, before the rite: the Great Toll is their name, forgotten by everyone who knew them, and they become the Seventh's new voice, retiring from ordinary adventuring. They may refuse; then no Toll is taken and the Concord doesn't happen. If they accept, they seat the Key unstruck and choose their final words. Read: "The Dreamer hears it, sighs, and begins to dream more gently."
plays.consequence: The world is restored, imperfectly. Dawns, harvests, storms, thaw, quiet dreams, and the dead remembered. The Ringer is the Seventh's voice.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer declines, offer the Second Dawn, or a postponement.
plays.tells: All six bells show as rung in the Forecast, and a player asks what the Great Toll means.
plays.rules: No ordinary Toll is paid at the rite; the six were paid when the bells rang. The Great Toll is never imposed.
plays.later: S28–30: every domain restored; the Stormwall thins to ordinary weather over a few years and Corvane joins the world. If someone sings the Cantor's verse, the Choir is released.
plays.keywords: concord, great toll, ringer, seat the key, chord, restore the world, best ending

plays.title: They strike the Seventh
plays.why: Corin's way, or desperation, or a wish to end the long unravelling for good.
plays.readAloud: The Hush cracks. Oum opens an eye, and the dream begins to unravel.
plays.response: The striker pays all six Tolls, disclosed first. Then the players talk with Oum, who asks direct questions and never lies: "Who is ringing my lullaby? Is the dream finished? Is it time to wake?" Pause for a table discussion. Unmake requires everyone's agreement; otherwise Remake, and each player names one thing that survives.
plays.consequence: Oum wakes. The world is remade from its best memories, or unmade into light.
plays.tells: A player asks what happens if they ring it, and means it.
plays.rules: Record all six Tolls for the striker (Memory, Year, Sense, Name, Fear, Gift).
plays.later: Remake: S28–30 rebuild scenes around what the players preserved. Unmake: one last night of farewells; skip years-later scenes.
plays.keywords: strike, ring the seventh, unbound, oum, wake, remake, unmake, ring ysh

plays.title: They seal the Key
plays.why: It costs no Toll and keeps every bell they rang.
plays.readAloud: You seal the Key into the Hush, unstruck, and the lullaby steadies. Above ground, the bells you rang are still ringing in the world. They are not enough to save everything, but they are enough to begin.
plays.response: One uninterrupted minute at the shrine's sealing recess. It stabilises only the domains whose bells were rung: name each one from the ring ledger. Unrung domains keep their afflictions. Releasing the Cantor still needs the verse.
plays.consequence: Partial restoration. Oum sleeps on.
plays.tells: Players ask what sealing does and whether it keeps the bells they rang.
plays.rules: Protect the minute: if a fight is still on, it's an action each round for 10 rounds by one character.
plays.later: If Thrane was rung, the Stormwall thins for good and Corvane opens to the world. S28–30 epilogues name only what was earned.
plays.keywords: seal, second dawn, recess, lock the key, stabilise, no toll

plays.title: The Court seals the shrine
plays.why: If the party is beaten or surrenders and Maudrin keeps the Key.
plays.readAloud: The Hush falls quiet again, not because you saved it, but because the Hushmen have sealed the stairs. The places you changed still bear your mark. Elsewhere, the collectors return to their rounds.
plays.response: This ending happens only if the group chooses to end its resistance. Otherwise play captivity, escape or a rescue chapter. Existing ringings still matter: the thaw, the storms and the quiet Sleepless persist.
plays.consequence: The Court rules on. The Tithe continues.
plays.fallback: Offer a rescue: the Stilled, the Choir, or a Stormborn crew comes for them.
plays.tells: The party is captured or retreating, and the Key is in Court hands.
plays.later: The Court keeps the Seam, and the memory trade grows. Survivors may resist in a later campaign.
plays.keywords: lose, defeat, surrender, empty choir, court wins, captured, sealed by court

plays.title: The chosen Ringer refuses the Great Toll
plays.why: Giving up your name and your character is a lot to ask, and refusing must stay a real option.
plays.readAloud: The bell waits. It has waited four hundred years; it can wait for you to be sure.
plays.response: Honour it completely: no Toll is taken and the Concord does not happen. The party may seal the Key, ask another willing character, postpone, or choose another course. Optional variant: Maudrin, if present and changed, offers to be the voice herself; this needs the party's agreement and makes the Concord about her penance.
plays.consequence: The Concord waits for someone willing, or doesn't happen.
plays.tells: A long pause after you explain the Great Toll in private.
plays.keywords: refuse, great toll, no, decline, ringer, sacrifice, won't

plays.title: They sing the Cantor's verse at the end
plays.why: If Ossa rang and the verse was learned, the finale is a natural time to free the Choir.
plays.readAloud: Far away, under a lake so still it holds the sky, a woman sings her own name, and stops singing.
plays.response: A sincere commemoration of a dead person, after Ossa rang, releases Ondra and the remaining Choir. If the verse was never learned, Mother Sallow can rebuild it from the restored ledger.
plays.consequence: The Drowned Choir is released.
plays.tells: Someone remembers the verse from Session 2.
plays.later: S28: Mother Sallow sings the last verse with Ila on the ferry-dock.
plays.keywords: verse, cantor, choir, release, sing, ondra, drowned

plays.title: They return to Pellmoor
plays.why: The story began on a dock with a girl and a humming bundle.
plays.readAloud: The Mere is so still the ships look painted on it, as always. On the oldest dock, a young woman in a ferry coat that finally fits her is counting the masts.
plays.response: Two NPC scenes and a closing question. Ila (if not Tithed) keeps the ledger and may become the ferry-folk's Ringer; Mother Sallow reads Davin's name aloud at last if Ossa rang; Brother Eld confesses, leaves, or is gone. Then the Landing: Brannagh, Sela, Venn, and what the Seam means now. Close on: "Who keeps the ledger now?"
plays.consequence: Act I's threads close.
plays.tells: Players ask what became of Ila and Mother Sallow.
plays.keywords: pellmoor, return, ila, mother sallow, epilogue, ledger, home

plays.title: They see the Stormwall open
plays.why: If Thrane rang and the ending stabilised it, Corvane is no longer hidden.
plays.readAloud: From the Pellmouth you can see it: where the wall of storm stood for four hundred years there is only weather now, grey and ordinary, and beyond it a sail, and another, and another.
plays.response: Over a few years the Stormwall thins to ordinary sea. The Landing Charter can't hold; ships go wherever they like. Ask each player what their character makes of a Corvane joined to the world: a Stormborn going home, a Bellfolk seeing the sea for the first time, a Lander staying for good.
plays.consequence: Corvane joins the Forgotten Realms in earnest.
plays.tells: Players ask what happens to the ships and the trade now.
plays.later: A hook for a next campaign: the Realms come to Corvane, and not all of them are friendly.
plays.keywords: stormwall, open, sea, ships, faerun, world, future, trade

plays.title: They decide who rules the Ninefold Shore
plays.why: With Maudrin gone or beaten, the Court, the Dawn Order and the Ironhorn all move.
plays.readAloud: Hallowmere’s terraces are full of people looking up, waiting to be told who speaks for them now.
plays.response: Rook (if she won the duel) leads a restored Dawn Order; Tristan Vesk wants the Chancellor's chair; Kessa, if alive, wants the Court's Tithe-taxes ended on the steppe. The party's allies and promises decide who gets the party's backing. Close on: "Who will rule the Ninefold Shore?"
plays.consequence: The Ninefold Shore has new rulers, chosen with the party’s weight behind someone.
plays.tells: Players ask what happens in Hallowmere.
plays.keywords: rule, court, chancellor, tristan, rook, kessa, hallowmere, future, government

plays.title: They return the Tithed memories
plays.why: With the Court broken, the vault of jars can finally be opened by their owners.
plays.readAloud: Bet Ostrow opens a small labelled jar in the grey vault, and smells bread, and finally knows why she has cried at that smell for seventy years.
plays.response: Owners who open their own jars get their memories back whole. Jonah remembers his mother's face if she is found; Lysse recovers what was filed under other names; Mother Sallow gets her wedding day back. Jars shipped abroad by the Coster are a thread for another day.
plays.consequence: The Tithe is undone, one jar at a time.
plays.tells: Players ask about the Blanks, Lysse, Bet or Mother Sallow's wedding day.
plays.keywords: jars, tithe, return memories, blanks, vault, restore, bet, lysse, jonah

page.title: CORVANE IN THE REALMS (v6 canon)
page.aliases: Forgotten Realms, Faerun, Faerûn, Sword Coast, Trackless Sea, Stormborn, Loudfolk, revision 6
page.body:
*Revision 6 canon. Where this page and v5 disagree, this page wins. The Canon Sheet (3.3) still governs every date and family line it lists.*

**Where Corvane is.** Corvane is a continent called **Hesk**, far out in the Trackless Sea beyond the last Sword Coast charts, part of the Forgotten Realms. A permanent band of storm circles it at sea, thirty to sixty miles deep: Faerûnian sailors call it **the Stormwall**, Corvanese who know of it call it **Thrane's Hem**. For four centuries no ship crossed it. Sword Coast sailors kept a legend of "the Ringing Land" west of the world; Candlekeep holds one water-stained portolan labelled *the Belled Coast*.

**DM truth: what the Stormwall is.** When Thrane fell silent on the Quiet Night, its storms did not end. They lost their shepherd and were pushed outward to the edge of the bells' resonance, where Ysh's lullaby stops. That is why no storm has crossed Brassfall in four hundred years: every storm Corvane should have had is in the Wall. Nobody knows this. Corin Aldeth suspects it; Edda Thorne's Notes imply it in one line ("Thrane's weather will go to the rim and wait").

**Before the Silence.** A few Faerûnian ships reached Corvane before the Quiet Night. Some of the Stilled in Glassreach are those sailors, frozen in 2 SS in Sword Coast clothes four centuries out of fashion.

**The Wrongweather (382 SS / 1462 DR).** The Ironhorn raid broke Old Garrow's sealed shafts. The dead lightning that poured out called to the storms at the rim, and for one night a storm tore up the river Pell onto the Mute Mere, the first weather the Mere had seen in 380 years. Davin Sallow drowned in it. When it passed it left a calm channel through the Wall: **the Seam**. At dawn the battered Baldur's Gate cog *Gull's Wager* drifted onto the Mere.

**Thirty years of contact.** Ilse Vesk's **Landing Charter** (384 SS) made Pellmoor the only lawful landing. Foreigners trade freely there but need a Court **writ of passage** to travel inland. Traffic has grown from one ship a year to forty or sixty a season. In come gold and silver, steel, paper, books, spices, wine, lenses and Lantanese clockwork (the Landing House removes every chime). Out go bottled memories (the richest export by far), glass-flowers, memory-pearls, reed-dye, bone-bound books and Ironhorn horses. Storm-stones and bronze are banned exports and smuggled anyway.

**Who is here.** The Vennmark Coster of Athkatla (Master Orsolo Venn), the Waterdhavian Corvane Venture, Baldurian factors, Lantanese gnome tinkers, Mirabar dwarves who want bronze, two quiet Harper agents, and Zhentarim memory smugglers. Lathander's Dawn Mission, a Kelemvorite shrine-tent and Chauntea's faithful; the Ninefold Church calls them "the loud gods."

**People and words.** Corvanese call Faerûnians **Stormborn** (polite) or **Loudfolk** (rude); Faerûnians call Corvanese **Bellfolk** or **the Quiet**; settled Faerûnians are **Landers**. Corvanese are mostly human, with halfling ferry-families, dwarven mining clans in Brassfall and very few elves. Dragonborn, tieflings, orcs, goliaths, gnomes and aasimar arrived with the ships, and Corvanese stare. Corvanese speak **Hesk**; Common is Pellmoor's second tongue.

**Magic.** Spells work by the 2024 rules. In Corvane every spell hums faintly as it is cast: that hum is Tonework, and it is how the Weave sounds here. Silence-stones suppress spells under the house rule in 2.6.

**Calendar.** 412 SS = 1492 DR.

page.title: THE STORMWALL AND THE SEAM
page.aliases: Stormwall, Thrane's Hem, the Seam, Pellmouth, river Pell, Wrongweather
page.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "Ahead, the sea stands up. A wall of black cloud and white water runs from one horizon to the other, lit from inside by lightning that never stops. And in it, like a door left open, a lane of grey calm a mile wide."
- **What it is:** a permanent band of storm thirty to sixty miles deep that circles Corvane at sea. DM truth: Thrane's lost storms, waiting at the rim of the bells' resonance.
- **The Seam:** the one calm channel through it, opened by the Wrongweather of 382 SS, in line with the mouth of the river Pell. A mile or two wide; it drifts with the seasons. Crossing takes about a day with a pilot who knows its moods.
- **The river Pell:** about forty miles from the Pellmouth inland to the Mute Mere. Two days by river.
- **Dangers:** drifting off the Seam. Ships that do are rarely seen again; pilots who come back describe a warm grey light at the storm's heart (see 11.7, the Edge of the Dream).
- **If Thrane rings:** the storms come home to Brassfall. For a season the Seam widens into a broad road and new fleets arrive within a month. If an ending stabilises Thrane (the Concord, or the Second Dawn with Thrane rung), the Stormwall thins to ordinary sea weather over a few years and Corvane joins the world.
- **Voyage:** about six weeks from Baldur's Gate or Waterdeep. Sailing season is spring (Ches) to early autumn (Eleint).

page.title: MEMORY AS MONEY
page.aliases: memory currency, keep, keeps, mote, motes, heartkeep, knowing, reckoner, gilding, exchange rate, coin, gold
page.body:
Corvane traded memories long before the ships came. The Court's Tithe made it a habit and the Reckoners made it a currency. Gold arrived thirty years ago and is winning, slowly.

**How it works**
1. **Drawing.** A memory can be drawn out of a person only with their consent, by a Court-licensed **Reckoner** with a tuning fork and a small stoppered vial of Mere-glass. It takes about a minute and feels like forgetting a word on the tip of your tongue, then not minding. Drawing without a licence is *leeching*, a crime.
2. **Keeps.** A drawn, sealed memory is a **keep**: a vial of faintly luminous mist that hums one low note when held. Reckoners grade it by **weight** (how much feeling it holds) and stamp the wax. The content stays private unless someone opens it.
3. **Keeps circulate sealed,** passed hand to hand like banknotes. Their value rests on two facts: someone will always pay to witness one, and its owner can always redeem it.
4. **Opening.** If the original owner opens a keep, the memory returns whole. Anyone else *witnesses* it, as a guest in someone else's day, without acquiring the owner's identity. Each stranger's witnessing fades it; after three it is a grey, spent vial.
5. **What cannot be drawn:** skills, spells, languages, proficiencies, anything a character can do. "You can sell the day you learned to swim, but never the swimming." Nobody can sell someone else's memory.
6. **Blanks** are people who sold or Tithed so many heavy memories that they no longer recognise their own families.

| Weight | What it holds | Worth at Pellmoor | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mote** | A passing memory: last Ossday's supper, a stranger's coat | about 1 sp | Grey wax. Small change. |
| **Keep** | A memory with feeling: a good afternoon, a small win | about 1 gp (floats daily) | Plain wax. The everyday coin. |
| **Heartkeep** | A defining memory: a parent's face, a wedding day | 25 to 100 gp or more | Red wax. The Tithe prefers them. |
| **Knowing** | Knowledge: a route, a recipe, a password, a face | by usefulness | Blue wax. The seller loses the knowledge. |

**Gold, and why the Court hates it.** Old Corvanese coin was iron "ticks" and Court scrip; bronze is bell-metal. Gold cannot be Tithed, cannot fade, cannot be Reckoned. At Pellmoor nearly every stall takes either. **Court taxes on Corvanese subjects must be paid in memory; foreigners pay the landing due in gold.** Paying a local's Tithe in gold is **gilding**: illegal and common. A keep fetches about 1 gp 2 sp at Pellmoor and about 8 sp in Hallowmere. The Hallowmere gate's courtesy memory is a registration, not a fee, and the clerk refuses gold.

**Table rules (2024)**
- A character may pay in memory wherever coin is accepted in Corvane. The player chooses the memory and writes one line in the Memory ledger (Foresight → Party & ledger). The DM never chooses it.
- A Reckoner buys memories at the posted rate less a 10 percent fee.
- Motes and keeps have no mechanical effect. When a character sells a heartkeep, the player rewrites one thing the memory held up (a belief, a bond, a fear). It never removes player knowledge or control of the character.
- The DM may award **Heroic Inspiration** when a character gives a memory freely to someone who needs it.
- Once, a character who witnesses a Knowing keep has Advantage on one ability check that knowledge plainly helps.
- Keep the kinds apart: a **Toll** can never be bought back; a **Tithe** can be redeemed from its jar; a **trade** is a keep; **Mere Memories** are borrowed; **eel bites** return after a long rest; **stairs** losses follow the stairs' rule.

page.title: THE LANDING (Foreign traders at Pellmoor)
page.aliases: Vennmark Coster, Corvane Venture, Harpers, Zhentarim, Landers, foreign traders, merchants
page.body:
- **Wants:** Profit, above all from bottled memories. An end to the Landing Charter's limits (or, for the Coster, an exclusive export licence). Safe passage through the Seam.
- **Fears:** The Court closing the Seam to them. A rival house winning the Court's favour. The Wall moving.
- **Methods:** Gold, credit, gifts to officials, hiring ferry-folk pilots, and buying memories in bulk.
- **Ideal:** *Prosperity.*
- **Members:** the Vennmark Coster of Athkatla (Master Orsolo Venn; the largest memory exporter), the Waterdhavian Corvane Venture (cautious, respectable), Baldurian factors, Lantanese tinkers, Mirabar dwarves after bronze. In the shadows: two Harper agents who distrust the Tithe, and a Zhentarim smuggling ring on Strangers' Row.
- **Secret:** The Coster buys "surplus" Tithed memories from the Court and ships them to Faerûn. The Tithe-Ledger has an EXPORT — VENNMARK column. Some Blanks' memories are in Athkatla.
- **How They React:** Warmly to customers, coldly to anyone who costs them money. They will not fight the Court, and they will not fight for it.
- **Clock move (at 6):** the Coster wins an export licence, a new fleet arrives, or a Zhentarim memory-smuggling ring is exposed.

page.title: 26. PILOT-MISTRESS BRANNAGH WICK
page.body:
- **Role:** Runs the Pilots' Hall on the Quays. Every ship that crosses the drowned town does it with one of her pilots. Tam Harrow was one of them.
- **Look:** Ferry-folk, about 60. Short, wind-cracked hands, a coil of sounding-line always over one shoulder.
- **Voice:** Gruff. Counts tides out loud. Calls every ship "she" and every captain "lad."
- **Wants:** The Hall kept independent of the Court and the trading houses. Ila safe.
- **Secret:** Tam took his boat out the night he died with no cargo and no ship to pilot, which no pilot does. She told the Landing House nothing. She thinks he was going to the Ossa Belfry, and she is right.
- **2024 stat block:** Scout (CR 1/2).
- **How She Reacts:** Trusts people who keep their word on the water. Will refuse a pilot to any ship she has a reason to stop, and every ship needs one to leave the Mere.

page.title: 27. RECKONER SELA MAUNT
page.body:
- **Role:** Court-licensed memory assayer at the Reckoning House on the Tally. The person who explains memory money to newcomers.
- **Look:** Corvanese, 40s. Grey apron, three tuning forks in a breast pocket, reading lenses bought from a Lantanese tinker.
- **Voice:** Precise, kind, slightly tired. Taps a fork against the counter when she thinks.
- **Wants:** Honest weights and a quiet life.
- **Secret:** She keeps a "Lost Shelf" of heartkeeps sold in grief and quietly lets the sellers buy them back at cost, which the Court forbids.
- **2024 stat block:** Commoner (CR 0).
- **How She Reacts:** Helps anyone who is kind to her: she can read a keep's weight, tell a forged keep from a true one, and explain gilding without saying the word. She will not appraise a bell's Tongue: "That's not a memory, love. That's a bell."

page.title: 28. MASTER ORSOLO VENN
page.aliases: Venn, Orsolo, Vennmark Coster, Gilded Heron, merchant, Amnian
page.body:
- **Role:** Factor of the Vennmark Coster of Athkatla, the largest memory exporter in Pellmoor. A human-sized antagonist of the memory trade.
- **Look:** Amnian, 50s. Plum velvet in a grey country, rings on every finger, a silent Lantanese pocket-clock he consults constantly.
- **Voice:** Warm, fluent Hesk with an Amnian lilt. Calls everyone "friend" and means "customer."
- **Wants:** An exclusive export licence from the Court. Curiosities from the Ringing Land for his buyers in Athkatla.
- **Secret:** He pays Tobias Quill to look away from certain cargoes. A buyer in Athkatla offers 5,000 gp for "a true bell-relic of the Ringing Land." The Coster buys Tithed memories from the Court for export, and its ledgers prove it.
- **The Gilded Heron:** the Coster's carrack, anchored beyond the last pier. Two Coster guards (Tough) on watch; a Baldurian crew who won't fight for the Coster.
- **2024 stat block:** Noble (CR 1/8), with two Toughs (CR 1/2) as guards.
- **How He Reacts:** Generous, then persistent. Prefers money to trouble and folds when a deal turns violent or public. Holds grudges in ledgers, not in alleys.

page.title: 29. SISTER AURELIE DAWNMANTLE
page.aliases: Aurelie, Dawnmantle, Lathander, Morninglord, Dawn Mission
page.body:
- **Role:** Morninglord priestess of Lathander who runs the Dawn Mission on Strangers' Row. Optional ally for clerics, paladins and anyone hurt.
- **Look:** Waterdhavian, 30s. Rose-and-gold vestments faded by the Corvanese light.
- **Voice:** Bright and earnest. Says "when the sun comes back" as if it were a date in a diary.
- **Wants:** A writ of passage to Hallowmere, to bring Lathander's dawn to a city that has none.
- **Secret:** The Court has refused her writ four times. She is close to trying without one, which would get her arrested.
- **2024 stat block:** Priest (CR 2).
- **How She Reacts:** If the party tells her about Vaer's bell, she becomes a devoted ally, and a liability, in Act II. Heals for a donation, or for a true story about a sunrise.

page.title: 30. BROTHER HADRIK VOSS
page.body:
- **Role:** Kelemvorite priest with a shrine-tent on Strangers' Row. Believes the restless dead of the Mere are an abomination to be laid to rest.
- **Look:** Grey robes, a skeletal-hand pendant, a censer he never lets go out.
- **Voice:** Low and certain. Quotes the Doomguide.
- **Wants:** To lay the Drowned Choir to rest, by force if need be.
- **Secret:** His own brother drowned at sea and was never found. The Mere's unrestful dead feel like an accusation.
- **2024 stat block:** Priest (CR 2).
- **How He Reacts:** Can be argued down from his own dogma: Kelemvor's dead are owed judgment and remembrance, not erasure (DC 15 Persuasion; a DC 12 Religion Study first grants Advantage). If he blesses the Mere during the Night Song, the Choir rises angry.

page.title: PELLMOOR LANDING: THE QUAYS, THE TALLY AND STRANGERS' ROW
page.aliases: Landing House, Reckoning House, Pilots' Hall, Strangers' Row, Loud Quarter, Brass Lantern, Quays, Tally
page.body:
**The Landing House (Quays).** Court customs. A grey stone hall with a silence-stone lintel. Writs of passage, the 5 gp landing due, cargo seals, and the chime-removal bench where every imported clock is silenced. Six Hushmen and Tobias Quill's office.
> **SAY:** "The clerk stamps your papers without reading them. 'Landing due, five gold. Pellmoor and the Mere road only. Anywhere else needs a writ from Hallowmere. They take about a season. Next.'"

**The Pilots' Hall (Quays).** A long reed-roofed shed built over the water, its floor a map of Old Pellmoor's drowned streets in painted planks. Brannagh Wick's pilots wait on benches for ships.

**The Reckoning House (the Tally).** A narrow shop with a slate by the door and a counter scored by tuning forks. Sela Maunt weighs keeps under a Lantanese lens. Behind a curtain: the Lost Shelf.
> **SAY:** "The slate by the door reads, in careful chalk: 1 KEEP = 1 GP 2 SP. MOTES AT 1 SP. HEARTKEEPS BY APPRAISAL. Underneath, smaller: NO GOLD FOR TITHES."

**Strangers' Row, the Loud Quarter.** Foreign inns, counting-houses, the Dawn Mission, a dwarven smithy, a gnomish clockmaker selling silent clocks, Brother Hadrik's shrine-tent, and music at all hours.

**The Brass Lantern.** The Faerûnian inn. Loud, warm, overpriced, and the only place in Corvane that serves Waterdhavian ale. The *Gull's Wager*'s old first mate drinks in the corner.

page.title: 2024 RULES NOTES (v6)
page.aliases: 2024, 5.5e, rules, Heroic Inspiration, Influence, Extreme Cold, Suffocation, Exhaustion, encounter budget
page.body:
- **Heroic Inspiration** replaces v5's "Inspiration."
- **Influence** (action): social plays use it. The DC is 15 or the creature's Intelligence score, whichever is higher; its attitude (Friendly, Indifferent, Hostile) decides whether a check is needed at all.
- **Study** (Intelligence) and **Search** (Wisdom) actions: clue scenes use them. Essential clues are never lost to a failed roll.
- **Extreme Cold** (Glassreach): end of each hour, DC 10 Constitution save or 1 Exhaustion level. Cold Resistance or Immunity succeeds automatically; so does a warm cloak or cold-weather gear (house rule kept from v5).
- **Exhaustion:** each level gives −2 to d20 Tests and −5 feet of Speed; a long rest removes 1 level; level 6 is death.
- **Suffocation:** hold breath for 1 + Constitution modifier minutes (minimum 30 seconds); out of breath, 1 Exhaustion level at the end of each turn, all removed when breathing again.
- **Frigid Water:** minutes equal to the Constitution score, then a DC 10 Constitution save each minute or 1 Exhaustion level.
- **Conditions** use the 2024 definitions. A Toll of Sense uses Blinded or Deafened.
- **Encounters:** Waypoint's Foresight computes difficulty from your roster with the 2024 XP budget per character (Low, Moderate, High). Corvane creatures have full 2024 stat blocks built on 2024 Monster Manual creatures; open them from any encounter.
- **Spells that touch memory** (Modify Memory, Greater Restoration, Remove Curse, Speak with Dead, Zone of Truth and others) have rulings in Foresight's anytime plays. Search "If they…" for the spell's name.

page.title: WHAT CHANGED IN REVISION 6
page.body:
**World.** Corvane is part of the Forgotten Realms, hidden behind the Stormwall until the Wrongweather opened the Seam in 382 SS (1462 DR). Pellmoor is now Pellmoor Landing, a port of about 4,000. Memory is a working currency alongside gold (MEMORY AS MONEY). New NPCs 26–30. New faction: THE LANDING.

**Act I.** New Session 1 opening (arrival at the port). Quill works from the Landing House and is short because Pellmoor pays in gold; H-03 can be solved by giving memories on the villagers' behalf. New Session 3 option: sell the Tongue to Master Venn (the *Gilded Heron* sails in three days). Optional complication: Brother Hadrik Voss blesses the Mere. Brannagh Wick is a fourth source on Tam's death; any two still establish the Court's responsibility.

**Act II.** Stormborn need a writ at the Hallowmere gate; the Chancellor's invitation counts. Optional reveal: the Tithe-Ledger's EXPORT — VENNMARK column.

**Act III.** Some Stilled are Faerûnian sailors from before the Silence. Glassreach uses 2024 Extreme Cold.

**Act IV.** Ringing Thrane loosens the Stormwall for a season. New Session 22 ally if earned: the Stormborn.

**Endings.** A stabilised Thrane thins the Stormwall for good; in the Empty Choir the Court keeps the Seam.

**Part 9.** Situation 17 now has ships home; Situation 18 has a sailor's dragon story; the Edge of the Dream lies inside the Stormwall.

**Rules.** 2024 throughout (2024 RULES NOTES). Full stat blocks and calculated encounter difficulty live in Foresight.

edits.find:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "Pellmoor sits on the gray shore of the Mute Mere like a dropped lantern. Reed-thatched houses lean toward the water. The ferry-dock creaks. Nets hang from poles like the sails of drowned ships. The chapel bell, which should ring, is silent. Across the water, the Mere is so still it reflects the sky perfectly, except where something beneath it moves."
- **Population:** About 300, mostly Ferry-folk.
- **Key locations:** the ferry-dock, the chapel (Brother Eld), Mother Sallow's reed-hut, the Harrow house, the net-racks, the ledger-house where the old names are kept, and the Inn of the Shuttered Bell.
- **Dangers:** The Drowned Choir sings at night. Hushmen visit once a week.
- **Secrets:** The chapel's cellar holds a rope that once rang Old Pellmoor's bell, and its end is still tied to something under the water.
- **Atmosphere:** Quiet, careful, mournful. Children do not play near water.
edits.replace:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "The Mute Mere is so still that the ships look painted on it. Forty masts stand over the water where a drowned town lies just beneath, rooftops like the backs of sleeping animals. On the Quays, a dozen languages argue over the price of a memory. Gnomes shout. Gulls do not; there are no gulls on the Mere. And at the far end of the waterfront, past the last warehouse, the old reed-roofed village of Pellmoor still leans toward the water as if none of this were happening."
- **What it is:** Corvane's only lawful port for foreign ships since the Landing Charter of 384 SS. Not a Court city: the Tithe Clock does not tick here. The Court is present through the Landing House and its six Hushmen.
- **Population:** About 4,000 year-round; nearly twice that in sailing season (spring to early autumn). Ferry-folk, Corvanese who came for work, and Faerûnian Landers.
- **The Old Shore:** the original ferry village. The old ferry-dock where Ila waits, the net-racks, the chapel (Brother Eld), Mother Sallow's reed-hut, the Harrow house, the ledger-house, the Inn of the Shuttered Bell, and the Mere Memory Shore. Foreigners are tolerated, not welcomed. Children still do not play near the water.
- **The Quays:** deep-water piers driven into Old Pellmoor's drowned roofs; warehouses, chandlers, a dry-dock; the **Pilots' Hall** (Brannagh Wick) and the **Landing House** (Tobias Quill; landing due 5 gp; writs of passage).
- **The Tally:** the market square. The **Reckoning House** (Reckoner Sela Maunt) posts the day's rate on a slate: *1 KEEP = 1 GP 2 SP. MOTES AT 1 SP. HEARTKEEPS BY APPRAISAL.*
- **Strangers' Row (the Loud Quarter):** the Faerûnian quarter. The Brass Lantern inn, the Vennmark Coster's counting-house (Master Orsolo Venn), the Corvane Venture hall, the Dawn Mission (Sister Aurelie), a dwarven smithy, a gnomish clockmaker selling silent clocks, a Kelemvorite shrine-tent (Brother Hadrik).
- **Dangers:** The Drowned Choir sings at night. Hushmen walk the Old Shore weekly and watch the Quays daily. Memory leeches and Zhentarim smugglers work Strangers' Row.
- **Secrets:** The chapel's cellar holds a rope that once rang Old Pellmoor's bell, and its end is still tied to something under the water. Every ship that leaves the Mere needs a Pilots' Hall pilot, so the ferry-folk can stop any departure.
- **Atmosphere:** Two towns in one. Loud, bright and foreign on the Quays; quiet, careful and mournful on the Old Shore.

**DO:** Use the Edge of the Dream (Part 11.7). It is a terrifying and beautiful place. Let the party explore it for one session. It can serve as a pre-Act V encounter or as an alternative ending.

**DO:** Let them, if they insist. Leaving pauses the plot: advance every faction clock by two for each month away, and send news of what the Court did in their absence. **The loud gods.** Thirty years of ships have brought Faerûn's faiths to Pellmoor. Lathander's Dawn Mission, Kelemvor's shrine-tent and Chauntea's wandering faithful are tolerated at the Landing and forbidden in Hallowmere. Their divine magic works in Corvane, humming like any Tonework. The Church calls them the loud gods and preaches that they are only another kind of noise.

**382 SS (1462 DR): The Wrongweather.** The dead lightning loosed from Garrow's broken shafts calls to the storms trapped at the rim. For one night a storm tears up the river Pell onto the Mute Mere, the first weather the Mere has seen in 380 years. Davin Sallow drowns in it. When it passes, it leaves a calm channel through the Stormwall: the Seam. At dawn the Baldur's Gate cog *Gull's Wager* drifts onto the Mere, the first Faerûnian ship in Corvane in four centuries.

**384 SS: The Landing Charter.** Ilse Vesk declares Pellmoor the only lawful landing for foreign ships and requires a Court writ of passage for foreigners travelling inland. Pellmoor begins to grow from a ferry village into a port.

**New in v6.** **Gilding:** paying a Corvanese subject's Tithe in gold; illegal. **Heartkeep:** a sealed defining memory, red wax. **Keep:** a sealed memory used as money. **Knowing:** a sealed memory that carries knowledge; the seller loses it. **Landing Charter:** the Court law that confines foreign ships to Pellmoor. **Lander:** a Faerûnian settled in Pellmoor. **Loudfolk, Stormborn:** Corvanese names for Faerûnians. **Mote:** a sealed trivial memory; small change. **Reckoner:** a Court-licensed memory assayer. **The Seam:** the one passage through the Stormwall. **The Stormwall:** the band of storm that circles Corvane at sea. **The Wrongweather:** the storm of 382 SS that opened the Seam. **Writ of passage:** the Court paper a foreigner needs to travel inland.
